articles.title: One Nation claims victory in Secret Harbour byelection in Western Australia
articles.summary:
One Nation candidate Luke Herdegen secures 57% of the vote after preferences as party’s WA leader says result will send shock waves across the country

One Nation has claimed victory in the…

blocks.text: One Nation has claimed victory in the Secret Harbour state byelection in Western Australia
With 74.5% of the vote counted, One Nation’s Luke Herdegen leads Labor’s Georgia Tree 57-42 after preferences.

One Nation’s WA leader Rod Caddies claimed victory at 9:30pm local time saying the result showed there were “no safe Labor seats in this state or in this country anymore” and that it would send “shock waves across the entire country”.
Voters in the safe Labor seat cast their ballots on Saturday after senior minister Paul Papalia’s mid-term retirement triggered the contest.
Luke Herdegen has been buoyed by a sea of orange across polling booths in the beachside electorate, south of Perth.
“The vibe has been really strong for the last six weeks,” he said.
WA Premier Roger Cook wasn’t throwing in the towel but conceded it would be a battle to hold the outer-suburban mortgage-belt electorate.
“It would break my heart,” he said when asked about defeat.
“By-elections bring up all kinds of opportunities for a whole range of issues to impact on the seat.”
On the ground in Secret Harbour, Labor was on the nose, with cost-of-living pressures, housing and a perceived lack of community amenities topping lists of voter concerns.
Local Luke Pors voted for One Nation and believes it will do a better job than either Labor or Liberal.
“We know what their true goal is and I think just in One Nation we trust,” he said.
The Qantas flight attendant was also impressed by Herdegen’s campaign.
“He’s like a home buddy and as obviously a youngie; we can really connect with him,” he said.
Retirees Ann and Les Scard also voted One Nation.
“It has been a pretty strong campaign by Luke Herdegen,” Les Scard said. “He deserves a chance.
“I get the impression Liberal and Labor are desperate; they’re doing everything to try and discredit them and I don’t think they’re being successful.”
Ann Scard isn’t concerned by One Nation’s controversial immigration policy.
“I agree with a lot of what Pauline Hanson says,” she said. “Something has to be done, it’s just all askew.”
Herdegen said people were desperate for change.
“They’re struggling with cost of living; there’s a major housing issue here with the mass immigration coming through and people have just had enough,” he said.
Retired truck driver Dean Maxwell isn’t so sure. He voted Labor.
“I didn’t vote for One Nation, I put them last,” he said. “I just don’t see any good policy.
“I don’t like any of the pollies but I particularly don’t like Pauline Hanson. I think she’s in Gina Rinehart’s pocket.”
One Nation’s performance in the tradie-haven will be of interest across the nation, particularly Victoria, which has a state election in November.

articles.title: Norway’s new King Haakon remembers ‘dear father’ Harald in first speech as sovereign
articles.summary: New monarch Haakon VIII paid an emotional tribute to his late father, Harald V, in his first address to the nation. Vowing to follow his own path, Haakon pledged to uphold Norway’s democracy, unity…

image.caption: Norway's new King Haakon VIII during his first speech to the nation at the Royal Palace in Oslo on August 29, 2026. Image: Heiko Junge/NTB/AFP

blocks.text: King Haakon VIII of Norway paid tribute to his late father, King Harald V, calling him "such a wonderful papa" in his first address to the nation as monarch.

"Above all, you were a person who remained committed to your values and dedicated to your duties," Haakon said Saturday in a televised speech. "We greatly mourn his loss. At the same time, it gives us consolation and strength to know that there are so many who are grieving with us."

Norway's King Harald died at 89, after more than three decades on the throne, during which time he became known as a reformer and a popular monarch. In a televised speech from the palace, Haakon praised his father as a "warm and devoted family man."
Haakon became emotional while speaking about his widowed mother, Queen Sonja. He noted that his parents would have celebrated their 58th wedding anniversary on Saturday.
Norway's King Harald V dies at 89

Earlier on Saturday, Haakon met at the palace with leaders of the Church of Norway, parliament and the Supreme Court. He also received Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, who viewed the late king’s casket after it was brought to the palace from Oslo University Hospital on Friday evening.
Flags flew at half-mast Saturday as mourners continued to gather at the palace, laying flowers alongside tributes left the previous day by more than 20,000 people.
Haakon stresses he will do things 'his own way'

Haakon said he would follow his own path, as his father did before him, while reaffirming the principles of Norway’s constitutional monarchy. He is due to swear an oath in parliament on Tuesday to uphold the country’s constitution and laws.
"We believe in our system of self-governance — and in democracy. We believe in a society built on the rule of law, where every individual has equal worth," he said.
Haakon automatically became king following his father’s death. Norway does not hold coronations, which were abolished by parliament in 1908.
But, like his father and grandfather before him, Haakon could opt for a consecration ceremony at Trondheim Cathedral, where Norwegian monarchs were crowned between 1814 and 1906.
The Norwegian prime minister told Reuters news agency that Haakon shared many of his father’s qualities, particularly his "ability to create an atmosphere of togetherness."

blocks.caption: Crown Princess Sonja and Crown Prince Harald, future King and Queen of Norway, with newly born Crown Prince Haakon in Oslo, Norway. [FILE: July 26, 1973]Image: TT/IMAGO

blocks.text: Mourning and challenges for the royal family

A national period of mourning has been declared, with no date yet set for Harald’s funeral. Churches across Norway will hold memorial services Sunday, including one in Asker, south of Oslo, which the royal family was scheduled to attend.
Harald was widely regarded as a symbol of an open and tolerant Norway and praised for leading a modern, modest monarchy.

The king had been hospitalized in Oslo since August 17 with hemolytic anemia, a condition that causes the rapid destruction of red blood cells and can lead to fatigue and shortness of breath. His health had deteriorated in recent years, forcing him to reduce his official duties.

blocks.caption: Haakon's wife, Mette-Marit, is under scrutiny for her ties to the late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. [FILE: 17 June, 2026]Image: PPE/IMAGO

blocks.text: The royal family has also faced a series of challenges. Haakon’s wife, Queen Mette-Marit, has come under scrutiny over her ties to the late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
In June, her son from a previous relationship was sentenced to four years in prison for two rapes, a sentence he is appealing.
Mette-Marit, 53, who has a serious lung disease, underwent a lung transplant in July.

articles.title: Palestinian woman and NBC News team reportedly attacked in West Bank
articles.summary:
Matt Bradley and crew assaulted while interviewing woman who said settlers had driven family out of home

A Palestinian woman and an NBC News team are reported to have been attacked and…

blocks.text: A Palestinian woman and an NBC News team are reported to have been attacked and injured by masked Israeli settlers in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Saturday, amid worsening confrontations in the area.
Benjamin Netanyahu said he condemned the violence committed “by a handful of rioters”.
The attack occurred when four members of the news team were interviewing Aida Ahmed Abdullah and her family in the Palestinian town of Jalud, near Nablus.
Abdullah told the outlet that they had been driven out of their home by settlers, and the team was walking down a hill toward the house.
A car with Israeli license plates reversed up the hill toward them. At least four men with their faces covered leapt from the vehicle, hitting them with sticks and throwing rocks.
“They jumped out, beat us, then jumped back in the car,” said NBC News correspondent Matt Bradley. Bradley was hit twice in the arm and treated at a nearby clinic.
Abdullah, 51, was taken for medical care by the Red Crescent. Her injuries were not life-threatening. Three other members of the news team were also injured and treated.
“Suddenly a car came to us,” said producer Lawahez Jabari. “The settlers had sticks, I saw a gun, but they didn’t use the gun.”
Camera operator Khaldoon Eid said the team had not expected to be attacked in a village.
Several violent incidents in the area were reported on Saturday. Palestinian workers were pepper-sprayed in nearby Qusra by masked Israeli settlers.
Israeli security forces told the outlet they had received reports that “violent clashes had occurred, including stone-hurling toward Palestinians and additional civilians”.
They said “security forces identified dozens of rioters who had barricaded themselves inside a Palestinian home while Palestinian residents were inside”, the statement said.

“The security forces who arrived at the scene initially operated to remove the rioters from the home and separate the groups, in order to protect the residents inside. In addition, the security forces confiscated vehicles belonging to the Israeli rioters that were suspected of having been used to reach the area,” the statement said.
“IDF soldiers and Israel Border Police forces continue to operate in the areas of Qusra and Jalud to prevent further disturbances and restore order in the area,” it added.

Earlier this month, a group of settlers began blocking supplies from entering Palestinian houses on the outskirts of the village near Nablus, trapping residents inside and drawing strong criticism from the US ambassador.
Israeli forces continue to operate in the area while settlers still roam the surrounding hills.

Netanyahu, whose government has been accused of turning a blind eye to the settler attacks, condemned the “criminal acts of violence” and blamed “a handful of rioters who violate the law, cause enormous injustice to the law-abiding settler public, hinder the IDF in fulfilling its missions and harm Israel’s standing in the world”.

According to the United Nations’ office for the coordination of humanitarian affairs, Israeli forces or settlers killed 76 Palestinians in the West Bank in the year to 24 July. Three Israelis were killed over the same period.

articles.title: Trump's Venezuelan oil deal: What we know and how it could impact Canada's oil industry
articles.summary: Several questions about the U.S. deal to develop vast Venezuelan oil reserves remain unanswered, and a rapid and large-scale increase in production is unlikely. But experts say increased exports from…

image.caption: A pedestrian passes a mural featuring oil wells in Caracas, Venezuela. Acting President Delcy Rodríguez said the deal with U.S. President Donald Trump's administration involves the development of 17 fields with a proven potential of 65 billion barrels of oil. (Pedro Mattey/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Besides a social media post from U.S. President Donald Trump, the White House has said little about what he is calling "THE BIGGEST OIL DEAL IN WORLD HISTORY" in Venezuela.

Trump said the agreement announced Friday night would give the United States a stake in Venezuela's vast oil reserves, a step toward his goal of extracting energy from the country after American forces captured then-president Nicolás Maduro in a middle-of-the-night raid in January and brought him to New York to face federal drug-trafficking charges.
Venezuela's acting president, Delcy Rodríguez, described the deal as a step toward economic recovery that will modernize the country's oil industry.
But the answers to questions such as how soon the reserves could be drilled and who will pay to make it happen were not immediately clear. No text of any agreement has been released.
Here's a look at what we know and don't know — and how the agreement could affect Canada's oil industry, too.
Trump announces Venezuela oil reserves will be controlled by U.S.
What are the terms?
The U.S. government and an unnamed private operator in Venezuela formed a new private company that was given the rights to vast, untapped oil fields for 100 years.

A statement from Rodríguez said the deal involves the development of 17 fields with a proven potential of 65 billion barrels. It said the agreement could draw $100 billion US in investment into Venezuela's oil industry and yield over $209 billion US in taxes for Caracas.

items: The facts about Venezuela in 60 seconds

blocks.text: Trump said the agreement was negotiated by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Rodríguez.

The deal gives the United States 55 per cent effective output of the new private company, including an ownership stake and rights to buy oil at cost. American purchases of the oil will go toward the U.S. strategic oil reserves along with the military, according to a U.S. official who was not authorized to discuss the matter publicly and spoke on the condition of anonymity.
The company would be the second-largest corporate holder of proven reserves after Saudi Aramco, according to the official.
Will gas prices go down?
Probably not any time soon.

Trump says the deal will help lower gas prices for Americans — an important objective for the Republican president as the Iran war slows the shipping of Persian Gulf oil and keeps prices elevated months before U.S. midterm elections in November.

But experts have repeatedly warned that Venezuela's dilapidated oil infrastructure will take years and billions of dollars to repair. A substantial boost in production is not expected to happen quickly.

The deal could be "helpful in the long run, but it's not going to do anything to change the price of gasoline at the retail station for Labour Day weekend," said Amy Myers Jaffe, director of the Energy, Climate Justice and Sustainability Lab at New York University.
Neither side made clear who would pay for infrastructure investments and at what cost.

Kevin Book, managing director at ClearView Energy Partners, said Venezuela has room to build on its oil production — in the past it produced more than 2.5 million barrels a day above current levels — but this kind of investment does not come quickly.
"It doesn't happen all at once. It's going to take time — many years — to deploy that much capital and produce the kind of incremental results that history suggests possible," Book said.
Trump pushes wary U.S. oil execs to move into Venezuela
What could the deal mean for Canada's oil industry?
While many details of the agreement remain unclear, experts said earlier this year that a revival of Venezuelan oil production would impact the Canadian oil industry.
Canada and Venezuela produce similar heavy crude, and over the past decades, Canadian oil filled a gap in the U.S. market amid shrinking Venezuelan exports.

U.S. imports of Venezuelan supplies "would compete directly with Canadian crude in the U.S. Gulf Coast market," Marc Ercolao, an economist at TD Economics, said in January after the U.S. said Venezuela would turn over as many as 50 million barrels of oil.
The Gulf Coast accounts for about 10 per cent of Canadian oil exports to the U.S., Ercolao said.
Observers say a rapid and large-scale increase in Venezuelan oil production isn't likely after years of under-investment, sanctions and political uncertainty.

items: Canada's economy has found its footing. But is it enough to survive the U.S. trade war?
Trump's trade war: Fact-checking Canada's natural gas leverage over the U.S.

blocks.text: But even a gradual recovery "would reintroduce meaningful competition into the North American heavy crude market," said Christopher Hernandez-Roy, acting director of the Americas program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, D.C.

Canadian heavy crude trades at a discount, or differential, relative to benchmark U.S. crude prices, Hernandez-Roy said in May. So a "meaningful increase in Venezuelan crude" could widen that differential and reduce the value Canadian producers get for every exported barrel, he said.

Over the long term, a significant scale-up of Venezuelan oil production also could strengthen Canada's push to diversify its trading partners and become less reliant on the U.S. market, the experts said.

"China, the number one buyer of Venezuelan crude, may need to strategically reorient their import sources, further buoying the case for Canada to diversify its energy trade," Ercolao at TD Economics said in January.
What questions remain?
The identity of the private operator, who will cover necessary investments and how America's stake in the company breaks down all remains unclear.
The U.S. will get 55 per cent of the company's effective output, but it was not clear what portion of that comes from the ownership stake and how much comes from the right to buy oil at cost.
It's also unclear how the industry will react. Persuading big American oil companies to return to the region could prove a challenge given the political uncertainty and damaged infrastructure.

items: Trump administration launches new bid to attract U.S. oil companies to Venezuela — but finding few takers

blocks.text: Chevron, the only U.S. oil company actively producing in Venezuela, declined to comment. Separately from Trump's announcement, Chevron already had been in talks to expand investment in the country. Exxon Mobil also declined to comment.
David Oxley, chief climate and commodities economist at Capital Economics, said that on its face the deal could double U.S. oil reserves and reduce dependence on crude oil from Canada and Mexico.
But Oxley, writing in a commentary, cautioned that there are logistical hurdles and he said the value of Venezuela's reserves may have been exaggerated under former president Hugo Chávez.

Even with legal and security guarantees, it is not clear that U.S. oil companies "would be eager to invest," he wrote, noting that "there simply might be more enticing commercial opportunities on offer elsewhere."

articles.title: Jenny Barzaga bags Dasmariñas congressional seat after son’s expulsion
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Incumbent Dasmariñas City Mayor Jennifer “Jenny” Barzaga has been proclaimed as the new congressional representative of Cavite’s fourth district, replacing her son, who was…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Incumbent Dasmariñas City Mayor Jennifer “Jenny” Barzaga has been proclaimed as the new congressional representative of Cavite’s fourth district, replacing her son, who was expelled for his unruly behavior by the House of Representatives on June 2, 2026.

With Barzaga’s victory effectively keeping the congressional seat within the family, the Barzagas’ political dominance in Dasmariñas will also continue, extending the dynasty’s hold over the city to nearly three decades since Elpidio “Pidi” Barzaga Jr. first became mayor in 1998.

Based on partial and unofficial votes as early as 8:30 p.m., Barzaga already led the special congressional race by a significant margin, placing first at 185,668 votes. The nearest rival was former vice mayor Raul Rex Rosario Mangubat, who, at this point, only garnered 23,208 votes.
Mangubat also eventually conceded based on the partial results alone, congratulating Barzaga on her win and expressing thanks to his supporters. /cb

articles.title: Turkish, Somali forces free vessel seized by pirates in Somalia
articles.summary: Turkish and Somali forces have freed the MV LUTUF after pirates hijacked the vessel off the coast of Somalia. The 10-day operation killed 14 alleged pirates and destroyed four boats used by the…

image.caption: Puntland Maritime Police Forces PMPF patrol against the pirate attacks off the coast in Puntland, Somalia [FILE: January 29, 2024]Image: Abuukar Mohamed Muhidin/Anadolu Agency/IMAGO

blocks.text: Turkey’s navy and Somali armed forces have freed a hijacked vessel in Somali waters and killed 14 alleged pirates following a battle that lasted several days, Somalia’s government said on Saturday.

"During the 10-day operation, four boats used by the pirates were destroyed and 14 pirates were killed," said a Somali Defense Ministry statement. "The sustained military pressure finally forced the remaining pirates to abandon the ship."

The MV LUTUF, a Cameroon-flagged vessel, was hijacked on August 17 off the coast of the Nugaal region of Puntland state. The joint Turkey-Somalia operation was carried out as part of a defense cooperation agreement between the two countries.

The ministry did not provide details about any casualties or the well-being of the crew aboard the vessel but said, "The forces subsequently secured the MV LATUF, which has now safely resumed its journey."
According to AFP news agency sources, at least eight members of the crew were on board, including one Turkish national.
Resurgence of piracy along Somalia’s coast
The Horn of Africa has seen a resurgence in piracy since April, according to figures from the International Maritime Organization, with at least 15 attacks off the coast of Somalia this year.
At least five cargo ships were held hostage, the most recent of which was seized on August 20 off Yemen.

blocks.caption: Maritime police patrol to ward off piracy off the coast in Puntland, Somalia [FILE: January 29, 2024]Image: Abuukar Mohamed Muhidin/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: These attacks are the highest since 2013. Piracy was rampant off the coast of Somaliain the 2000s. It peaked in 2011 before being curbed by international naval deployments and new protection measures for commercial shipping.

The resurgence of piracy in the Horn of Africa is adding to mounting challenges for international shipping in the Middle East, where vessels are already navigating around the contested Strait of Hormuz and seeking to avoid Houthi attacks in the Red Sea.
In recent years, pirate attacks have also increased along the West African coast, adding another layer of risk for commercial shipping.

articles.title: Buck Martinez inducted into Blue Jays' new Hall of Excellence at Rogers Centre
articles.summary: John Albert (Buck) Martinez, a cancer survivor, catcher, manager and broadcaster for parts of five decades with the Toronto Blue Jays, was inducted into the club's new Hall of Excellence on Saturday.

image.caption: Buck Martinez speaks to the crowd and former Blue Jays greats before being inducted into the team's new Hall of Excellence during a ceremony before a game against the Mariners at Rogers Centre in Toronto on Saturday. (Jon Blacker/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: MLB·Updated
John Albert (Buck) Martinez, a cancer survivor, catcher, manager and broadcaster for parts of five decades with the Toronto Blue Jays, was inducted into the club's new Hall of Excellence on Saturday.
11 honourees from the former Level of Excellence were also enshrined in the hall
· The Canadian Press
· Posted: Aug 29, 2026 4:22 PM EDT | Last Updated: 16 minutes ago

As part of their 50th season celebrations, the Blue Jays unveiled the section to honour the franchise's greatest contributors. The 11 honourees from the former Level of Excellence were enshrined in the hall, located on the concourse behind right field at Rogers Centre.

The 77-year-old Martinez was honoured before the Blue Jays' matinee against the Seattle Mariners. His popularity across Canada exploded during his lengthy stint as a team broadcaster, a position he retired from last winter.
"Today blew me away," Martinez said. "I didn't have any grasp of the magnitude of today."

items: 'A swing and a drive' for Buck Martinez as Blue Jays induct him into Hall of Excellence this weekend

blocks.text: Martinez added he was also blown away when newcomer Brett Bateman stopped him underneath the stands to congratulate him, saying he knew what Martinez meant to the Blue Jays and their fan base.
He also told a story of visiting England in July. Martinez was having a beer with a friend when a group of ladies walked by. They circled back to say hello because they recognized his voice.
He made a point of saying how much Canadians meant to him.

"First thing they tell you is where they're from," Martinez said. "They say I'm from New Brunswick. I'm from Calgary. I came in from Winnipeg. They're so proud that they came this far to watch the Blue Jays, and that's the impact the Blue Jays have had on this entire country."
Martinez joins Jose Bautista, Paul Beeston, George Bell, Joe Carter, Tom Cheek, Carlos Delgado, Tony Fernandez, Cito Gaston, Pat Gillick, Roy Halladay and Dave Stieb in the hall.

The Level of Excellence will remain on the fascia within the ballpark bowl through the remainder of the season. It will be relocated next year within the stadium's bowl, where the names will remain visible to fans.
Toronto Blue Jays unveil new Hall of Excellence

The Californian, who now lives in Florida, flew north to Toronto on a plane with Gaston and Bautista. Delgado, Bell, Carter, Stieb, Beeston and Gillick helped open the new hall and take in Martinez's ceremony.

"He was an awesome teammate," Stieb said at a morning media availability. "He was especially special for me because, as you know, I was quite a battler out there. I would lose my emotions at times, and Buck just had a knack for calming me down and keeping me focused on the task at hand."

Building on the legacy of the Level of Excellence, the hall will provide a space to honour players, coaches, managers, builders and broadcasters - past, present and future - to bring generations of fans closer to the people who shaped the Blue Jays, the team said.

Martinez was a Blue Jays catcher (1981-1986) and manager (2001-2002) who enjoyed two stints as a team broadcaster (1987-2000, 2010-2025). The fan favourite was diagnosed with head and neck cancer in April 2022 and lung cancer in May 2025.
He went 100-115 before being let go as Toronto's manager in May 2002. As a catcher, he was constantly asked about a play in game at Seattle on July 9, 1985.

In the bottom of the third inning, Martinez tagged out Phil Bradley on a throw from right-fielder Jesse Barfield. But Martinez broke his leg and dislocated his ankle in the violent collision at the plate.

Still, a seated Martinez tried to throw out advancing runner Gorman Thomas at third. But his toss sailed into left field, where George Bell threw a strike back to the injured catcher for a memorable 9-2-7-2 double play.
"I picked up the end of the stretcher to help carry him off the field," Bell said. "He was yelling at me in pain. It turns out his 1/8broken 3/8 leg and ankle were rubbing against me."

"It was an incredible play," Stieb added. "To have your leg broken and still have the wherewithal to try to throw somebody out was unbelievable." Martinez retired as a player in 1986 after a 17-year Major League Baseball career with the Blue Jays, Kansas City Royals and Milwaukee Brewers.
Called over 4,000 Blue Jays games
His broadcasting career began in 1982 while still an active player for the Blue Jays. Martinez started by covering playoff games and the all-star game for the Telemedia Radio Network.
He began his television broadcasting career in 1987 as a colour analyst and went on to call over 4,000 Blue Jays games over his career.

His final appearance in the broadcast booth came last fall when he called the World Series with longtime broadcast partner Dan Shulman on Sportsnet. The Los Angeles Dodgers defeated the Blue Jays in the deciding seventh game.

items: Commentator, former Blue Jays catcher Buck Martinez announces retirement

blocks.text: Martinez has also provided commentary for ESPN, XM Radio, TBS, The Baseball Network, TSN, and MLB International over his career.
In 2023, he was awarded the Canadian Baseball Hall of Fame's Jack Graney Award for his significant contributions to baseball in Canada.

articles.title: Jenny Barzaga wins Dasmariñas congressional seat, replacing expelled son Kiko
articles.summary: With Jenny Barzaga set to assume the congressional seat, her other son, incumbent Vice Mayor Thirdy Barzaga, will replace her as city mayor
articles.byline: Axel Cainglet, Miriam Grace A. Go

blocks.text: CAVITE, Philippines – Last-term Dasmariñas Mayor Jenny Barzaga won the special congressional election in the city to replace her son Kiko Barzaga, who was expelled by the House of Representative for disorderly behavior, conduct unbecoming of a member, and violations of the House’s Code of Conduct.
The Commission on Elections (Comelec) proclaimed Barzaga at past 3:21 am on Sunday, August 30, a day after the special poll.

Barzaga garnered 201,893 votes, commanding a huge lead over her four rivals, including former vice mayor Raul Rex Mangubat and former councilor Jacinto “Jesse” Frani Jr., who got 30,373 and 24,350 votes — the second and third highest numbers — respectively.

Mangubat had conceded his bid as early as 7:42 pm on Saturday. In the 2025 congressional election, Frani gave Kiko Barzaga a close fight, losing by only around 15,000 votes. Historically, that margin is slim for any Barzaga candidate.

With Jenny Barzaga’s victory to assume the congressional seat, her other son, incumbent Vice Mayor Thirdy Barzaga, will replace her as city mayor, while the vice mayoralty seat will be filled in by 2025 polls’ top councilor Rudy Lara.
Jenny had been congresswoman before, swapping posts with her husband, the late Elpidio Barzaga Jr., each time they reached their term limits as mayor and district representative.

The Comelec reported a 57.75% turnout, with 258,361 of the 447,387 registered voters braving the heavy rains on Saturday, August 29, to cast their vote. This means Barzaga captured 78% of the votes cast.

In the morning of the special election, Comelec Chairman George Garcia had said that voter turnout in Dasmariñas in regular elections were usually at 65% at the least, but that, given the inclement weather, “Masaya na tayo kung mag-50%” on Saturday (We’d be happy if it hits 50%). Cavite, among other areas in Mega Manila, experienced heavy rains on Saturday.
The rains were so bad that the Comelec en banc unanimously decided to extend the voting by two hours, from 3 pm to 5 pm.

Still, the special voting hours very early in the morning — 5–7 am — indicated that Dasmariñas constituents were intent on casting their votes despite the bad weather. The two-hour window, exclusive to the elderly, persons with disabilities, and pregnant voters, saw more than 25,000 votes already cast, Garcia said.

“Yung mga kababayan natin kahit sobrang lakas ng ulan, nandun pa rin sa labas ng gate ng mga paaralan. Ang unfair naman na hindi sila makakaboto kasi sinuong nila ‘yung ulan kaya napagdesiyunang i-extend nang dalawang oras man lang,” Garcia said.

(Our fellowmen are outside the gates of the schools despite the heavy rains. It would be unfair to stop the voting after they braved the rains, so we decided to extend the polling hours for even just two hours.)

Aside from the weather, voters had to contend with disinformation during the early hours of the voting. An AI-generated video circulated, making it appear that Frani had dropped out of the race. He immediately denied it through a statement in his Facebook page.
At the voting centers, Dasmariñas residents shared with Rappler their needs that they wanted their new legislator to help address. These included targeted basic services, like healthcare and housing.
Maria Ignacio, 53, said housing should be prioritized, particularly for those who face threats of demolition in the creekside area in Barangay Burol 2.
“Ang amin lang naman ay may malipatan kami. Basta maayos na malipatan na di na kami papaalisin. Para nang sa ganun wala na kaming pangamba,” said Ignacio.
(We only want a place to permanently settle in. As long as it’s a safe place where we will no longer be evicted. We don’t want to live in fear [of eviction] anymore.)
Meanwhile, 73-year-old Salvacion Ballesteros said ensuring free medical services should be prioritized by the next district representative. – Rappler.com
Axel John Cainglet is a political science student at the University of the Philippines Manila. An Aries Rufo Journalism Fellow for 2026, he is also the editor-in-chief of The Manila Collegian.

articles.title: Nova Scotia father and son haul hooked bald eagle out of lake, safely free it on shore
articles.summary: Bryan Esbaugh and his 15-year-old son, Wyatt, were fishing on Ponhook Lake in Queens County, N.S., when they accidentally hooked a bald eagle. After safely untangling the bird on shore, they set it…

image.caption: The bald eagle accidently got caught on a father and son's fishing lure Friday morning. (Anne-Marie Charron-Esbaugh)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia·New

Bryan Esbaugh and his 15-year-old son, Wyatt, were fishing on Ponhook Lake in Queens County, N.S., when they accidentally hooked a bald eagle. After safely untangling the bird on shore, they set it free and playfully dubbed it the "Canadian White-Headed Lake Raptor."
'Canadian White-Headed Lake Raptor’ pokes fun at Trump’s recent renaming orders
Bryan Esbaugh and his 15-year-old son, Wyatt, were fishing for smallmouth bass on Ponhook Lake in Queens County, N.S., on Friday morning when they accidentally caught a bald eagle.

“We saw this bald eagle following us around the lake. So we thought, 'Oh, it must be waiting for us to catch a fish to see where they all are,'” said Wyatt, who used to feed bass to birds while fishing with friends.

For about half an hour, the eagle followed them along the shore and skimmed the water for breakfast. When the eagle circled back around for one last sweep of the lake, it grabbed their fishing lines and lures out of the water and flew away.
“It seemed to get all tangled up in the line and it crashed in the middle of the lake,” said Bryan. “... It was flopping around and waving all over the place.”
They steered their boat toward the eagle and noticed one of the hooks piercing in its beak while another caught its foot. Wyatt hauled the eagle out of the water and into the boat.
“We were trying to stay away from it because of its big claws.… It's probably 25 pounds or so,” Bryan said.

They eventually made it back to the dock, but as they were getting out, the eagle flopped back into the lake and drifted away. Wyatt quickly manoeuvred the boat and guided the eagle to shore. He wrapped the bird in a towel, held it down, and together they removed the hooks.
Dr. Jessica Rock, a veterinarian with the Cobequid Wildlife Rehabilitation Centre, said while it’s not uncommon to treat birds tangled in fishing gear, lures and ropes, this case was unique.

“They did sort of the best in their arsenal that they knew how to do, and certainly they did help this animal,” said Rock. “We would recommend if they encounter a situation like this again in the future that the animal is seen just to make sure that they have the best chance of success.”
She recommends contacting the Department of Natural Resources to help with any future entanglements.
“Even though bald eagles look really big and strong, they're actually quite delicate in a lot of interesting ways, and so having somebody who's really experienced handling them can be a big help.”
In the end, the eagle managed to fly free.
“Our dog chased it a little bit to kind of get it to fly away," said Bryan. Then off flew what they named the "Canadian White-Headed Lake Raptor."
Bryan said calling the American symbol a "Canadian White-Headed Lake Raptor" is a tongue-in-cheek response to Donald Trump attempting to rename Lake Ontario.

articles.title: August reveals Australians’ big appetite for weight-loss drugs, love for ‘dupe’ brands and an accelerating EV uptake
articles.summary:
Reporting season shows how consumers are responding to cost of living pressures and how retailers are responding

  • Get our

blocks.text: Australians are buying less pizza but more weight-loss drugs. They love “dupes” but don’t enjoy writing letters.
Here are five key takeaways from the August reporting season that show what consumers are buying as cost of living pressures reignite, and how retailers are responding.

items: 1. Anko everywhereKmart’s home brand, Anko, started out with a strategy of mimicking popular items, like Birkenstocks and Skims, at a fraction of the price.The “dupe” strategy that won over the masses is expanding, and going upmarket.The Wesfarmers-owned Kmart Group, which includes Target, generated $11.7bn in sales last financial year, underpinned by Anko, according to its annual results.Anko has moved into furniture and is pitching itself as a rival to Ikea through its new K home store. Meanwhile, there are now six Anko-branded stores in the Philippines run via a joint venture, and further global expansion on the horizon.The biggest strategy change in recent months has been what the retailer describes as “one-up and two-up” price tier categories, whereby Anko offers an entry-level product and a couple of higher quality – and higher priced – options to entice those who like more stylish dupes.

2. Pizza vouchersDomino’s Pizza has long been popular for budget conscious families and penniless teenagers, with value deals aplenty.That has started to change, with the pizza chain reducing its level of discounting, in a move designed to improve profitability for franchisees and investors. While revenue dropped more than 11% from its Australian and New Zealand operations over the past 12 months, it believes the new model will help its franchisees operate more sustainable businesses.Domino’s is the fourth biggest fast food chain by store numbers, in Australia after Subway, McDonald’s and KFC, data from analytics company GapMaps shows.Sign up for the Breaking News Australia emailBut the pizza chain is in a tricky place given it is trying to reduce discounting at the same time as cost of living pressures reignite.It is hoping its new tie up with Coca-Cola, replacing Pepsi from September, may pay dividends as customers respond to a new and expanded drinks menu.

3. Weight boomSigma Healthcare-owned Chemist Warehouse is cashing in on weight loss drugs in unexpected ways, as sales of appetite altering GLP-1 drugs grow.Sigma’s chief executive, Vikesh Ramsunder, told analysts after the company’s earnings result that customers buying GLP-1 drugs, like Ozempic, are also putting other products such as protein powders into their shopping baskets because rapid weight loss can also lead to muscle loss.Interestingly, those taking weight loss drugs are also buying more beauty products.“It’s really about the fact that we’re selling products linked to individuals who are taking these medicines that they probably feel better, so they buy more kinds of beauty products and more healthcare-related vitamins and supplements,” Ramsunder told analysts.All up, the shopping basket size of a GLP-1 customer is 40% larger than those not buying weight loss products, according to Chemist Warehouse data.

4. Electric salesThe electrification of Australia’s car industry is in full swing, accelerated by high petrol prices caused by the Iran conflict.Eagers Automotive, operator of the largest network of car dealerships in Australia, noted in its financial results that once a driver steps away from a full combustion engine, they rarely go back.“The one thing we have observed is that the transition from a fully combustion engine car to a full electric vehicle – and that transition might include a hybrid vehicle, a plug-in hybrid vehicle, and ultimately a full battery electric vehicle – is a one-way street,” the chief executive of Eagers Automotive, Keith Thornton, told analysts. Almost one in three new vehicles sold in Australia during July was electric, with combined battery-electric and plug-in hybrid sales reaching a record 32% of new car sales, according to the Electric Vehicle Council.EV sales are now running about triple the volume from a year ago.

5. Snail mailThe government-owned Australia Post reported a pre-tax loss of $108m for last financial year, as rising delivery costs and the existential decline of letter sending weighs on its finances.Letter volumes are now at 1930s levels, when Australia’s population was about one-quarter the current size. Today, most letters are sent by businesses and government agencies.The problem for the postal service is that the cost of maintaining a national delivery system is getting more expensive at the same time as letters are phasing out, with volumes falling a further 15% during the last year alone.To partially offset costs, Australia Post is increasing the price of a basic stamp by 15c to $1.85 on 1 September. Stamp price increases have been extreme – it cost 70c just over a decade ago to send a regular letter – raising questions over how much longer snail mail will exist.

articles.title: Tennessee governor says he backs airport name change to honor Dolly Parton
articles.summary:
Bill Lee says he favors proposal to rename Nashville’s international airport after legendary country singer

Bill Lee, the Tennessee governor, on Friday said he favored a proposal to rename…

blocks.text: Bill Lee, the Tennessee governor, on Friday said he favored a proposal to rename Nashville’s international airport after legendary country singer Dolly Parton, who died three days earlier at age 80.

In a statement, Lee said he and the managers of the airport in Tennessee’s capital city – where Parton resided – wanted to create “a lasting tribute to her indelible legacy and the generations of people she inspired”. He said he had spoken previously to the 11-time Grammy winner and her team, who were “touched by the idea”.
“Dolly Parton’s extraordinary life is forever woven into the fabric of our state,” Lee said, noting that Nashville airport is where Tennessee welcomes the world.

He added: “It is fitting that Nashville International Airport would bear the name of our state’s favorite daughter and greet travelers with the enduring legacy of Dolly’s music, generosity, faith, and kindness.”

The proposal was scheduled to be addressed at a meeting of the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority (MNAA) on 17 September. A statement from Doug Kreulen, MNAA president, said the Nashville airport shared Parton’s understanding that “dignity, kindness and opportunity should never be defined by where you come from or your socioeconomic status”.
“Whether you are boarding a private aircraft or taking your first flight, you deserve to be welcomed, respected and served with the same level of care,” he remarked.

Parton had requested a private funeral for immediate family, and there is not going to be any public memorial. She will be buried beside her husband, Carl Dean, at Nashville’s Woodlawn memorial park and mausoleum.

The singer told Entertainment Weekly in 2014 that she expected Whitney Houston’s rendition of I Will Always Love You to be part of her service. Parton also said she wanted an old gospel hymn, If We Never Meet Again, which was her father’s favorite.

In a video statement announcing her death on Tuesday, Parton’s nephew Bryan Seaver, her longtime head of security, remarked: “Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton because, after a life wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest.”

Lee discussed the proposal to rename Nashville’s airport after a plane tugging a banner urging the name change buzzed over the Tennessee state capitol on Friday. A petition was also launched, and it has since gained more than 150,000 signatures.

“Everybody is looking for a way to honor Dolly and her legacy,” petition organizer Dan Dion told the Tennessean. “Our airport is so important, and there’s symbolism in flying into Parton Airport. With Dolly’s message of love, acceptance, music, kindness, humor and all these things, people feel that she is representative of what Tennessee truly is.”

If it comes to be, renaming Nashville airport will be at least the second airport in a matter of months to make a switch. Palm Beach airport was recently renamed for Donald Trump, with mixed reactions from travelers and locals about naming the facility after the president.

Freddie O’Connell, the Nashville mayor, hinted that the proposed name change is only the start of metropolitan tributes in the city. He said the 9 to 5 and Jolene singer had been in the process of developing a hotel and museum called SongTeller “that she called her love letter to Nashville”.
“Now it’s our turn to share a love letter to Dolly – by renaming Nashville International Airport to Dolly Parton International Airport in Nashville,” O’Connell told the Tennessean.
He also said the city was “working closely” with Parton’s team and family “on appropriate public recognition”.

articles.title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinian homes in West Bank
articles.summary: Masked Israeli settlers launched their first major attack since initiating a siege in the village of Qusra earlier this month. Saturday's attacks were met with rare criticism from Prime Minister…

image.caption: Israeli settlers reportedly followed trapped Palestinians into a home, attacking them with rocks and pepper sprayImage: Jaafar Ashtiyeh/AFP

blocks.text: Masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, pelting them with rocks and trapping residents in their homes.
The incident was the first major attack by Israeli settlers since they began a siege in the villages of Qusra and neighboring Jalud earlier this month.

On Saturday, settlers descended on Qusra and began pelting Palestinians with rocks. When dozens of residents sought to barricade themselves in a home, settlers followed them in, according to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF).

"The security forces who arrived at the scene initially operated to remove the rioters from the home and separate the groups, in order to protect the residents inside the house," said an IDF statement.
Palestinian group watches for Israeli settlers in West Bank
Who is the IDF protecting in such situations?
Although the IDF said settler vehicles had been impounded and authorities were gathering evidence, Palestinian media said the IDF protected the settlers during the melee.
A number of Palestinians said they were injured after being pepper sprayed by settlers, and reported that other Israeli settlers had tried to burn nearby fields owned by Palestinians.
One Palestinian said the IDF had fired tear gas into the home that he was in and held several people inside while at the same time letting Israeli settlers go free.
Other Palestinians said IDF officers had handcuffed, blindfolded and beaten residents trapped inside before letting them go.
Local Palestinians told international news teams that they had been trapped in their homes for hours waiting for help from the IDF.
The IDF did not comment on the use of tear gas nor accusations of handcuffs and beatings.
Saturday attacks elicit rare criticism from Netanyahu
Saturday's attacks took place just yards away from three other Qusra homes that radical Jewish settlers targeted in a siege that began three weeks ago.
Despite a massive Israeli military presence that local Palestinians say has kept them imprisoned in their houses, residents report near-daily settler encroachments.

Rights groups say settler aggression is part of an — illegal — effort to seize land from residents in the occupied West Bank, where Palestinians hope to one day found their own independent state. The Israeli government has rejected accusations of illegality. Various Israeli political figures have justified the settlements for security reasons or argued there are biblical grounds for the creation of the settlements.
The IDF has said it will continue "to operate in the areas of Qusra and Jalud to prevent further disturbances and restore order in the area."

Although settlers have been emboldened by the stance of Israel's far-right government — which has encouraged settlement building despite broad international opposition — the Saturday attack managed to elicit rare criticism from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

On Saturday, Netanyahu released a statement on X saying, "I strongly condemn the criminal acts of violence committed in the villages of Qusra and Jalud by a handful of rioters who are violating the law, causing a grave injustice to the law-abiding Jewish community, interfering with the IDF in carrying out its missions, and harming Israel's standing in the world."

Increasing Israeli settler violence has even garnered criticism from US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, who recently denounced radical settlers in the West Bank as "Israeli terrorists," adding that those behind the siege of Qusra could face US sanctions.
Palestinian American watches as West Bank house under siege

articles.title: AFP warns of 'foreign malign influence' riding on Sara Duterte trial, local issues
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Saturday warned of a growing trend in which foreign malign influence operations are riding on local issues, including the ongoing impeachment trial of…

blocks.text: Published August 30, 2026 3:54am

The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Saturday warned of a growing trend in which foreign malign influence operations are riding on local issues, including the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte and concerns over flood control projects.

Speaking at a forum, AFP spokesperson retired Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad said these operations had gradually shifted their focus over the past four to six months from pro-China narratives to issues affecting the country.

"As Congressman (Robert Ace) Barbers mentioned earlier regarding the impeachment, and (Col. Francel Padilla) noted regarding bots and technology—these are all interconnected. The trend for the past four to six months shows that malign information messaging is now riding on local issues," he said.
Trinidad said the trend was expected to persist until 2028, which would coincide with the end of the Marcos administration.

“Before, it was focused on the West Philippine Sea, pro-Davao, or pro-China narratives. Now, it is harder to detect because it is riding on the impeachment, Sanjia, and flood control issues,” Trinidad said.

Trinidad was referring to the Philippine Sanjia-Steel Corp., a steel manufacturing company operating in the PHIVIDEC Industrial Estate in Tagoloan, Misamis Oriental, which became a national-security and political issue after authorities raided the facility on May 15, 2026, arresting around 69 Chinese workers and one Filipino.

Prosecution team adviser and spokesperson Robert Ace Barbers, who also attended the forum, urged the public to carefully evaluate information encountered online and, whenever possible, examine the actual evidence presented during the impeachment trial.
“Fake news circulates every day,” he said.
Barbers said lawmakers who endorsed Duterte’s impeachment also appeared to have been targeted by misinformation.
"Not only that. All those members of Congress who endorsed the impeachment against the Vice President are also in the crosshairs of fake news peddlers, so they are included," he said.
"Because I think if they cannot address the issue with substance, they resort to personal attacks against those individuals instead. That is one of the strategies we have observed," Barbers added.
The former lawmaker again urged the public to closely follow the impeachment proceedings and assess the evidence presented during the trial to guard against online misinformation.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: LAPD releases footage of death of man whom police handcuffed and beat
articles.summary:
Jose Carlos Hoyoz-Munoz was arrested after a family altercation and restrained for ‘combative’ behavior

A cadre of Los Angeles police officers beat and restrained a handcuffed man in July,…

blocks.text: A cadre of Los Angeles police officers beat and restrained a handcuffed man in July, minutes before he was found dead in a jail cell, according to newly released body-cam footage.

On 15 July, Jose Carlos Hoyoz-Munoz, 58, was found unconscious in his cell at the Van Nuys regional jail. At the time, the LAPD said two use-of-force incidents had occurred, without specifying the nature. In the video released on Friday, the department said three use-of-force incidents occurred.

Body-cam footage showed Hoyoz-Munoz flapping what appeared to be a piece of cloth against the window in his holding cell. Several officers entered the cell and pinned him to the ground. The department described the restraint as being spurred by Hoyoz-Munoz’s “combative” behavior as they sought to fingerprint him.

The officers placed him in a harnessed chair, which they used to transport him to the booking stalls, the video shows. Police used the weight of their bodies to restrain him again, citing resistance. The department said Hoyoz-Munoz also spat at officers, after which they put a spit hood over his face.
Hoyoz-Munoz was escorted back to his cell. He was still handcuffed with the spit hood partly covering his face and his pants sagging down to his ankles, exposing his backside.
After climbing on top of a toilet, officers again entered the cell. They moved him to the cell bed, piling on top of him as he was positioned face down.
The department said officers conducted wellness checks for 20 minutes afterward, when he appeared to exhibit signs of life.
Later, an officer saw that Hoyoz-Munoz was not moving. He was found unconscious and not breathing when they checked on him.
Hoyoz-Munoz was arrested on 13 July, when police received a call about a suspected assault with a deadly weapon. Hoyoz-Munoz allegedly injured his mother and another relative with a knife.
Upon arrival at the scene, an officer encountered Hoyoz-Munoz’s mother with a laceration on her arm.
“He has lost his mind. He’s gone crazy,” she said in Spanish.
Another family member had a wound on his arm.

After an hours-long standoff with law enforcement, during which Swat agents deployed teargas, an agitated Hoyoz-Munoz was located in the residence, kneeling before a piano as he touched the keys and spoke of religion.
Los Angeles police also released video showing the death of 33-year-old Alejandro Luis Garcia, whom officers fatally shot. Garcia had allegedly shattered car windows with a baseball bat.

Los Angeles’s mayor, Karen Bass, described both videos as difficult to watch in a Friday statement. She called for an independent evaluation into officer-involved deaths concerning people experiencing a mental health crisis.

“People who experience behavioral or mental health crises often do not receive the proper care they desperately need. Without it, they can deteriorate into behavior that can result in severe injury or death,” the mayor said.
“We must rigorously examine whether our policies, training, tactics, supervision and accountability systems are sufficient.”

articles.title: Former Ecuadorian president imprisoned for corruption
articles.summary: Lenín Moreno denies taking bribes from a Chinese firm to secure a contract to build a hydroelectric plant.

blocks.text: A former president of Ecuador has been sentenced to five years in prison after being found guilty of taking bribes.
Lenín Moreno insisted he had not taken money from a Chinese firm which secured a contract to build a hydroelectric plant in the Latin American nation.

The 73-year-old will serve his sentence under house arrest due to his age and disability, and has already indicated his intention to appeal against the verdict after a court in the capital, Quito, found him and 19 others guilty of corruption.
Moreno, who was president between 2017 and 2021, is the third former Ecuadorian leader to be sentenced for corruption.

Prosecutors alleged that that Sinohydro, which is owned by the Chinese state, paid a total of $76.1m (£56.2m) through shell companies to people involved in the deal to secure the construction of the Coca Codo Sinclair hydroelectric dam.
Among those handed prison sentences were Moreno's wife, daughter and brother, as well as former plant managers, Sinohydro representatives and a Chinese ambassador to Ecuador.
While Moreno himself was alleged to have received very little from the scheme, prosecutors said family members received tens of thousands of dollars.
Those convicted of bribery will have to repay three times what they were given, while Moreno was barred from public office.

He denied involvement in the alleged bribery scheme and instead blamed another former president, Rafael Correa, under whom he served as vice-president and who was sentenced to eight years in prison in a separate bribery case in 2020.
Moreno argued that Correa had signed off on the Coca Codo Sinclair project, and that he had launched an investigation into issues with the construction when he had assumed the presidency.

The Ecuadorian government launched legal proceedings against Sinohydro in 2021 due to cracks appearing in the dam and other technical failures. It reached a $400m settlement with the firm's owner earlier this year.
The BBC has approached Sinohydro and the Chinese embassy in Ecuador for comment.

articles.title: Norway's new king remembers 'my dear father' in first speech
articles.summary: Haakon VIII pays emotional tribute to his late father, Harald V, before outlining how he wishes to reign.

blocks.text: Haakon stressed national unity in the speech, saying the royal family believed in a "society built on law and justice, where everyone is of equal value".

He said Harald had been a good father to himself and his sister, Princess Märtha Louise, as well as a "warm and funny grandfather" to his six grandchildren and a "loving and caring husband" to his widow, Queen Sonja.
The new king appeared to choke back tears as he noted that Saturday would have been their 58th wedding anniversary.
Harald brought the family together "with a natural authority", of which he might not have been aware himself, his son recalled.
He had "always stayed true" to his "values and commitments", the new king stressed.
"He constantly reminded us in the family that each of us must do things in our own way. Find our own style. Be ourselves," Haakon said.
He also remarked on the "powerful and moving experience" of seeing thousands of Norwegians gather outside the royal palace in the capital Oslo with "flowers, tributes and candles".
"We are in mourning, yet at the same time it brings comfort and strength that so many are grieving together with us," he said.

Norwegians have been laying flowers outside the royal palace in Oslo since news broke that Harald had died on Friday. A national period of mourning has been declared, with no date yet given for his funeral.

Among them was Norway's Prime Minister, Jonas Gahr Støre, who laid flowers outside the palace and signed a book of condolences after greeting the new king, said the country was "united in grief and gratitude".

Haakon will swear an oath of allegiance in parliament on Tuesday and will later participate in a consecration service with his wife, Queen Mette-Marit - a stripped-down version of a coronation, which Norway no longer holds.
He assumes his new role at a difficult time, as the royal family has faced health challenges and scandals this year.
Mette-Marit came under scrutiny when it was revealed that she had had a three-year friendship with the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, for which she publicly apologised.

She later received a lung transplant, after suffering from pulmonary fibrosis since 2018. Doctors will not declare her stable until next year, meaning her husband must balance his new official duties with her care.
Her son from a previous relationship, Marius Borg Høiby, was convicted in June of rape and other offences and sentenced to four years in prison. He is appealing.
Høiby is not a member of the royal family, but was raised with them since he was four years old, when Haakon married his mother.
Haakon's sister, Märtha Louise, has also courted controversy for remarrying an American self-styled shaman in 2024, their business activities ultimately leading her to step back from royal duties.

Without directly referencing these controversies, Haakon said during his speech: "Our family has experienced the importance of standing together in order to remain steadfast both within ourselves and for one another even during difficult times."
He said he, along with Mette-Marit and Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra, would "always strive to understand the life situations of different people".
He added: "No one who lives in this country knows what we will face together, but what we do know is that we will stand by one another through both good days and difficult ones."
Although Harald remained popular until his death, a poll for newspaper Aftenposten earlier this year suggested that support for the monarchy had dropped from 72% in 2024 to 54%.

However, Norwegian royal experts told the BBC that the new king, while facing questions about the turbulence surrounding his family, was respected, hard-working and, they believed, able to move forward despite the challenges.

articles.title: Australia usually hosts the world's biggest cuttlefish mating event - not this year
articles.summary: According to official figures only 1,811 cuttlefish turned up to mate this year, down 97% on last year.

blocks.text: Every winter, a sliver of the South Australian coast hosts the world's largest mating event for giant cuttlefish.

Some years, hundreds of thousands of the unique marine species endemic to Australia gather along the Cuttlefish Coast for the annual mating season, bringing their colourful, shape-shifting figures to the shallow waters and attracting thousands of keen divers.
But this year, the turnout was the lowest on record, sparking concerns of a "catastrophic decline" of the species.
Official figures released this month estimate just 1,811 cuttlefish turned up to mate this year, down from 63,000 last year - a 97% drop.
The state government says a toxic algal bloom that has ravaged the state's coastline for more than 18 months may be to blame for the sharp decline.
The low figures have also prompted calls for the species to be listed as endangered.

Adult cuttlefish typically die after breeding so each mating season is crucial for the species' future, but in recent months, just 440 eggs have been counted, instead of the millions that are usually laid.

Manny Katz, 28, was one of four divers who spent hours along the coast last month to observe the annual breeding event, having been tasked by South Australia's Department of Environment and Water (DEW).

"Because there have been so few cuttlefish, DEW thought it would be worth going out and trying to do an assessment of how many eggs there currently are around the coastline to understand what the population is going to be next year."
Over two days in July, his team did eight one-hour dives, exploring the undersides of rocky reefs to count the eggs.
"Along the eight kilometres (five miles) of coastline, there would normally be millions of eggs," he said, as each female can lay dozens of egg and tens of thousands usually turn up to breed.
"[We] pretty much looked under every single rock that we could have and we only found about 440 eggs."
While it's too early to tell what this means for the species' future, Katz said: "we will know that answer probably in the next year or two, whether or not this year has been a catastrophic decline."
His team also tracked adult cuttlefish numbers during the dive survey, and said the dozen or so they saw - when there should have been tens of thousands - appeared to be behaving differently.
"This year, they were all really skittish... hiding under rocks. Because there's so few cuttlefish hanging out at the moment, they don't have strength in numbers."
Katz said he wasn't shocked by the low numbers this winter given the devastating impact of the toxic algal bloom in South Australia since it was first detected in March last year.

The algal bloom - a rapid increase in the population of algae in water systems – is naturally occurring but is caused by ocean warming, marine heatwaves, and nutrient pollution - all exacerbated by climate change.

"Our marine habitats have been getting wiped out for the past year and a half now... this is an indicator that our marine ecosystems are in real big trouble - the canary in the coal mine, so to speak."

Last year's cuttlefish mating season was not impacted as the effects of the algal bloom had not yet reached the Cuttlefish Coast, Katz said, but since late last year, small concentrations of the toxic algae have been detected in the area.
This was particularly worrying as cuttlefish, along with other cephalopods like octopus and squid, are particularly vulnerable to the toxic algae.

Stefan Andrews, co-founder of the Great Southern Reef Foundation, is seeking to have the giant Australian cuttlefish listed as a threatened species given its "catastrophic decline" due to the algal bloom and the impact on the next generation.

"The harmful algal blooma is a leading plausible explanation and appears likely to have contributed, but the vailable evidence does not yet allow us to say definitively that it caused the entire decline," he said.
He said with so few adults and so little breeding activity observed, the number of young entering the population is likely to be very low.
"That will make the next breeding season especially challenging."
A spokesperson for South Australia's Department of Primary Industries and Regions said cuttlefish populations "naturally fluctuate" depending on environmental conditions.
Previous surveys have reported record lows of 13,500 in 2013 to highs of 247,000 in 2020.
"The cuttlefish population estimate rebounded to more than 100,000 just two years following the low numbers in 2013," the spokesperson said.

"While it appears likely the algal bloom has impacted cuttlefish numbers, researchers are working to determine whether this contributed to the reduced population or was just one of the potential impacts."

Prof Mike Steer, executive director of the South Australian Research and Development Institute which helped carry out the underwater surveys, said the unprecedented low estimate this year was "disheartening".
But he remained hopeful as "we know from the past that this population has the capacity to recover when conditions are favourable".
He said there were "positive signs" as adult cuttlefish were continuing to lay eggs and the population may recover "over coming years".

articles.title: Great Deals bets big on ‘AI commerce’
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — In a social media-crazed country such as the Philippines, e-commerce has grown by leaps and bounds, overcoming even the constraints of an archipelagic market where distance and…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — In a social media-crazed country such as the Philippines, e-commerce has grown by leaps and bounds, overcoming even the constraints of an archipelagic market where distance and logistics have long complicated the movement of goods.

But for one homegrown e-commerce giant, that growth, driven largely by the emergence of platforms such as Shopee, Lazada and TikTok Shop, may pale in comparison with what could come next when artificial intelligence (AI) enters the picture.
And that does not mean simply automating responses on shopping apps.

Great Deals E-Commerce Corp., a homegrown e-commerce enabler that helps brands sell their products online, believes the next big opportunity lies in “AI commerce”—where AI agents do the selling and, eventually, even help consumers do the buying.

“As of now, humans are still better sellers than AI. But that does not mean AI cannot sell. It can sell. It can produce revenue,” Great Deals founder and CEO Steve Sy says as he scrolls through an e-commerce feed populated by both human livestreamers and AI agents modeled after the looks and voices of actual employees.
Banking on that potential, Great Deals is already positioning itself for what Sy describes as the “next frontier” of Philippine e-commerce.

Inside the company’s otherwise unassuming headquarters in Quezon City, there is already a nook lined with computers and monitors churning out round-the-clock livestreams featuring AI-generated sellers hawking products on digital shopping platforms.
Automated live-selling
Great Deals currently has around 20 AI livestreamers, alongside about 50 human live-sellers. Sy says the company wants to increase the number of AI sellers to about 60 by the end of the year.

And that is not simply an attempt to ride the AI boom. Sy prides himself on being an early adopter of the technology and sees a practical use for it in a business where keeping products in front of shoppers for longer can translate into sales.
While he acknowledges that human sellers remain better at appealing to shoppers on a personal level, Sy says AI can do something people cannot: keep selling continuously.
On a single account on one platform, a Great Deals AI livestreamer generated P730,217 in sales over 241 hours.

But Sy also notes the apprehension about the technology, including among some of the brands that Great Deals serves. The company, therefore, makes it explicit when a livestreamer or piece of content is AI-generated rather than human-made.
Not humans vs AI
Within Great Deals itself, however, Sy takes pride in cultivating an AI-receptive workplace where people are not pitted against machines.
“We have a blended culture,” Sy says. “It’s human talent plus an AI-powered assistant. It’s not just a workflow; AI agents are teammates already.”
And while Great Deals’ AI live-selling push was introduced only this year, it is already adding another revenue stream to a business headed for what could be another banner year in 2026.

According to the company, it had already generated P10.6 billion in revenues in the first seven months of 2026, up 28 percent from a year earlier. Gross profit grew even faster at 34 percent, while operating expenses retreated by 11 percent.
With that performance, Great Deals is targeting P20 billion in revenues for the full year, which will surpass the record-high P15.4 billion recorded in 2025.
“We had our best year last year. And then, this year is going to be better,” Sy says.

That will continue the e-commerce company’s rapid expansion from P4.4 billion in revenues in 2020 and about P12.4 billion in 2024. Great Deals ultimately wants to grow revenues to P100 billion by 2030.

It sells products for more than 500 brands across e-commerce platforms such as Shopee, Lazada and TikTok Shop. Among its largest clients are Nestlé, P&G, NutriAsia, Del Monte, Unilever and Maybelline New York.
Regional expansion

Even with its rapid growth, Sy says another fundraising round remains on the table as Great Deals looks beyond the Philippines and aims to add more “firepower” to acquire larger companies as it expands across the Asia-Pacific region.

Recall that in 2021, Great Deals secured $30 million in a Series B funding round led by local logistics major FAST Group of the Chiongbian family. Before that, in 2020, it secured $12 million in Series A funding from private equity firm Navegar.

Sy says the company could pursue a Series C round once it has acquired two to three companies, which he says would demonstrate that its acquisition and integration strategy works. The intent is to raise more than $100 million, he says.
An initial public offering (IPO) likewise remains part of its longer-term plans, although Sy stresses the timing and venue will depend on market conditions.
“We do have ambitions to be listed. We want to have an IPO in the future, definitely,” Sy says.

If and when Great Deals decides it is ready to brave the public market, Sy says his own ambition is to list on the Nasdaq. But he does not write off a listing on the Philippine Stock Exchange, which he says the company may reconsider if the GCash IPO planned for October does “very well.”
Even before then, Sy says Great Deals is already preparing itself to go public.
“When the opportunity comes, we’re ready,” he adds. INQ

articles.title: Employees turn entrepreneurs for a cause
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — For one day, doing business at Security Bank Corp. meant more than ringing up sales. Employees behind small businesses sold their products at the Frederick Dy-led bank’s annual…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — For one day, doing business at Security Bank Corp. meant more than ringing up sales.
Employees behind small businesses sold their products at the Frederick Dy-led bank’s annual People’s Fair Marketplace, knowing that every booth also carried a chance to help someone stay in school.

The marketplace formed part of Security Bank’s 75th anniversary celebration, turning employee entrepreneurship into support for the Security Bank Foundation’s “Regalo Mo, Kinabukasan Ko (RMKK) Scholarship Program.”
Held at the SMX Convention Center Manila, the fair gathered businesses run by Security Bank employees.
Participation fees paid by exhibitors were donated to the foundation to help fund the education of deserving but underprivileged students.
For the employees who joined, it gave an ordinary marketplace a different purpose.
Kimberly Malka Soner, a relationship manager from the corporate banking group, says learning where the booth fees will go made participating even more worthwhile.
“It’s a great opportunity to sell while giving back,” Soner says.
That support goes to a scholarship program that is now running in its 16th year.
RMKK provides educational assistance to Security Bank’s agency-hired personnel, including janitors, security guards, messengers, drivers and other support staff, as well as their children.
For the academic year 2026 to 2027, the program is supporting 87 scholars, extending educational opportunities to families with limited financial means.
For Jan Jethro Puzon, another relationship manager from the corporate banking group, the fair also brought something personal to the table.

“I have always believed in giving back—whether through my personal life, our church, or simply helping others when I can,” says Puzon. “Joining the People’s Fair was a chance to support a cause I care about while also cheering on my wife’s baking business.”
That combination—employees becoming entrepreneurs while helping students—has made the annual marketplace an expression of generosity within the bank’s community.
Along with the Security Bank Foundation’s “Adopt a Scholar” campaign, proceeds from the initiative help finance scholarships.

“The People’s Fair gave us the chance to showcase our products, connect with the Security Bank community, and at the same time support initiatives that help students achieve their educational goals,” shares Jose Gil Puey IV, an information technology officer.

For the scholars themselves, business banking segment officer Tristan Joseph Legaspi had a simple message: remain persistent, keep pursuing education and trust that the determination to finish their studies will eventually pay off.
“Keep your persistence and drive for continuous education, and remain hopeful that your determination to finish your studies will eventually be rewarded,” Legaspi enthuses.
The public can also contribute to RMKK through the foundation’s Adopt a Scholar campaign.
Established in 1951, Security Bank is marking its 75th anniversary this year. The universal bank operates across retail, corporate, commercial and business banking, among other financial services.
But at its anniversary marketplace, the currency was not limited to money changing hands.
For employees, every booth fee became something that could last beyond the fair itself—a little more help toward keeping a student in school and, perhaps, opening the door to a brighter future. INQ

articles.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: Nepal calls for technical support for rescue efforts as number of missing rises to nearly 3,000 – latest updates
articles.summary: Nepali government says India and China are sending expert tunnel rescue teams, as minister estimates cost of rebuilding could be billions of dollars
articles.byline: Keely Aouga (now); Nadeem Badshah, Taz Ali and Wendy Frew (earlier)

blocks.text: Nepal government calls for specialised assistance from neighbouring countries to aid rescue efforts
The Nepalese government has requested “specific and specialised assistance” from neighbouring countries to aid search and rescue efforts.

This includes assistance with opening tunnels where people are trapped, technologies that can help locate people alive in affected areas, rapid forensic and DNA analysis, and mortuary facilities for the proper storage of bodies, Nepal’s ministry of foreign affairs said in a statement.
It added: “An 11-member specialised technical reconnaissance team for tunnel rescue from India has been mobilised and a tunnel rescue team from China is expected to arrive very soon.”
