articles.title: James Cleverly resigns from shadow cabinet to run for mayor of London
articles.summary:
Shadow minister for housing, communities and local government to resign with immediate effect

James Cleverly has resigned from the shadow cabinet to run for mayor of London.

The Tory…

blocks.text: James Cleverly has resigned from the shadow cabinet to run for mayor of London.
The Tory heavyweight, who was once home and foreign secretary and is shadow minister for housing, communities and local government, told the Sunday Times he will resign with immediate effect.

The MP for Braintree, who lost his bid to lead the Conservatives to Kemi Badenoch, is considered a more moderate voice in a party that has lurched to the right. On breaking the news to Badenoch, Cleverly told the Sunday Times: “She took it very well. Kemi has been very gracious.”

He added: “Our route to getting Kemi in No 10 has got to be through success in London,” he said. “It’s a business city, entrepreneurialism, arts, culture. I don’t buy the lazy idea that London is a Labour city. It represents the philosophical heart of the Conservative party.”
Cleverly’s resignation comes in advance of the Conservative party conference in October, where he is expected to make his case to party members.

According to the Sunday Times, sources close to Badenoch said she was “gutted” about the news but added that she “is delighted that someone of his calibre wants to put himself forward to be Conservative nominee for mayor of London”.
Cleverly had kind words for Badenoch. “Frankly, Kemi is doing really well now. She’s getting great cut-through. It took longer than any of us would have liked, but she’s getting it,” he said.

Sadiq Khan is halfway through his third term as mayor. He has not stated whether he will run for a fourth term in the contest to be held in May 2028. Susan Hall was the Tory candidate in 2024 but lost to Khan, who was declared the winner with 43.8% of the vote.
If Khan does step down, the Labour MP for Brent Central and Brent South, Dawn Butler, is expected to throw her hat in the ring, having previously revealed her desire for the job.

Cleverly is the most senior Tory politician to run for mayor of London in recent times. Making his bid, he said Khan was “asleep at the wheel” and accused him of using the role as a stepping stone for a higher-profile position.
after newsletter promotion

“Sadiq has been trying to get out of that job for quite a while. He went in with the intention of doing what Boris [Johnson] did, using it as a high-profile platform to get him his next big job in government. There has been lots of posturing, very little delivery. Lots of picking rows with the president of America, less focus on bringing down street crime. It wouldn’t surprise me if he bows out for 2028. He’s lost the passion for the job.”

Days before Keir Starmer stood down as prime minister, he handed Khan a peerage, potentially opening the door to him joining Andy Burnham’s cabinet in future. However, while Burnham and Khan have worked closely together over the years and have a shared understanding of the challenges of devolution, it is understood Khan has told the former Manchester mayor that he has no wish to be a minister in his government.

articles.title: Russian-American heads Trump's planned Caucasus trade route
articles.summary: A Russian-born businessman heads the investment fund financing the so-called "Trump Route," a planned corridor through Armenia linking Azerbaijan with Nakhchivan. Who is Konstantin Sokolov, and what…

image.caption: The proposed 'Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity' would follow the path of a former Soviet railway, near the border with IranImage: Anthony Pizzoferrato/Middle East Images/picture alliance

blocks.text: Until recently, few people in the South Caucasus had heard of Konstantin Sokolov. Now the 52-year-old Russian-American businessman is at the center of new investment fund backed by US President Donald Trump.

In mid-July, Sokolov — who emigrated from Russia to the US at age 21 and later founded the investment firm IJS Investments in Chicago — was appointed to head a new investment fund of the US State Department.

The TRIPP+ EnterpriseFund, registered in the US as the Trans-Caspian Enterprise Fund and launched with more than $200 million (about €172.5 million) in capital, is expected to invest in countries across the South Caucasus and Central Asia and help finance the large-scale TRIPP infrastructure project, also known as the "Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity."

The "Trump Route" is a transit corridor that aims to connect Azerbaijan with its autonomous exclave of Nakhchivan through Armenian territory. The ambitious infrastructure project is part of a peace deal that Armenia and Azerbaijan signed in August 2025 with US mediation. In early June 2026, Washington and Yerevan signed a framework cooperation agreement for the project.
Experts have said construction of the "Trump Route" fits Washington's strategy of creating a trade corridor between Europe and the region that bypasses existing routes through Russia and Iran.
Sokolov buys up Russian assets in Armenia
Long before he was appointed to head TRIPP+, Sokolov had already established a foothold in Armenia.

In 2024, he acquired Viva Armenia, the country's largest telecommunications provider. Despite its subsequent partial nationalization, Sokolov continued to expand his holdings. Recently, his companies also bought up the Armenian subsidiary of Russian telecom giant Rostelecom.

blocks.caption: In August 2025, Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev (left) and Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan (right) signed a joint declaration 'peace road map' after talks with TrumpImage: Azerbaijan Presidency/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: An even more significant deal, however, was carried out largely out of the public eye: the purchase of the Teghut copper-molybdenum mine. The mine, which holds an estimated 450 million metric tons of ore and has Armenia's second-largest reserves, had been taken over by Russia's state-owned VTB Bank after the company accumulated massive debts. VTB is now under Western sanctions. According to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty's Armenian service, the deal was carried out through a third-party company.
"Sokolov wanted to avoid a direct deal with the Russian bank," said Mkrtich Karapetyan, a Radio Liberty journalist who has been investigating the flow of foreign capital into Armenia.
Sokolov: Trump supporter, MAGA backer
While Armenia's government and its supporters have welcomed the influx of Western capital into the country's infrastructure projects, the opposition has highlighted serious risks.

Mesrop Manukyan, a lawmaker from the opposition Armenia Alliance, is among Sokolov's most vocal critics in parliament. He said it's alarming that a US investor has been able to acquire major stakes in the finance, mining and telecommunications sectors in just a few years.

Manukyan's faction, which advocates close ties between Armenia and Russia, opposes the TRIPP+ project. It views the "Trump Route" as a disguised "extraterritorial corridor" and the "greatest threat" to Armenia's security.
Armenia looks to EU after decades of relying on Russia

Despite his extensive investments, Sokolov remains largely unknown to the Armenian public. There are no official photos of him, and he generally avoids interviews with the local press during business trips.

His most recent visit to the capital, Yerevan, was in early August, when he met with Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan. He was accompanied by Aryeh Lightstone, senior adviser to US special envoy Steve Witkoff.

In Western media, however, Sokolov is known not only for his business ventures in the US and Switzerland but also for his political involvement. Sokolov is a major donor to the US Republican Party and a Trump supporter. According to The Associated Press, he donated about $11 million to Trump's MAGA movement over the course of a year.
'Compromise' between Moscow and Washington?
Benyamin Poghosyan of the Armenian think tank APRI sees two main reasons for Sokolov's appointment to head the fund.
The first is political. Appointing an American with Russian roots could be "a subtle gesture by Washington aimed at easing Moscow's fierce criticism of the project," he told DW.

The second, however, is pragmatic. "Perhaps Russia has nothing to do with it at all. Sokolov may simply have been chosen because he has a deep understanding of the business environment in the former Soviet Union — and because he knows Armenia and how its government works," said Poghosyan.

blocks.caption: Armenia and Azerbaijan were locked in a conflict over the Nagorno-Karabakh region for decadesImage: Tofik Babayev/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: At the same time, the sheer scale of the investment and the financier's Russian roots are fueling speculation in Armenia. Social media users in the country are debating whether Sokolov, who was born in St. Petersburg, could be a secret "compromise figure" between Moscow and Washington. Supporters of the theory point to the ease with which US companies have acquired formerly Russian assets subject to Western sanctions.

Other observers have refuted the idea, noting that Sokolov has publicly and sharply criticized the Russian government and its war against Ukraine. The funds provided by the US State Department, running through 2036, are seen as flagging Washington's long-term strategic intentions in the region. During his visit to Yerevan, Aryeh Lightstone told Armenian news outlet CivilNet that the more than $200 million in initial funding could be viewed as a starting point for future investments.

Aram Sargsyan, head of the Republican Party of Armenia and an ally of Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, also rejects the idea that Sokolov is a "compromise figure" for Moscow. He emphasized the practical value of Sokolov's background, seeing it as an opportunity rather than a cause for concern.
"Sokolov has significant business contacts, understands the Russian mentality perfectly, speaks the language and knows how to work with relevant Russian institutions," he said.
This article was originally written in Russian.

articles.title: Saxony-Anhalt election: Why the AfD is so strong
articles.summary: The AfD is polling above 40% ahead of Saxony-Anhalt's election on September 6. What is driving support for the far right in this predominantly rural eastern German state?

image.caption: Though the AfD has been classified as a 'confirmed right-wing extremist' organization, this has done little to dent its popularityImage: Klaus-Dietmar Gabbert/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Saxony-Anhalt, one of Germany's 16 federal states, boasts a rich cultural and historical heritage.

Many of the world-famous architects associated with the Bauhaus in Dessau lived and worked here. The towns of Eisleben and, above all, Wittenberg preserve the memory of the great reformer Martin Luther. It was in Wittenberg that he famously nailed his 95 theses to the door of the Castle Church, setting the Reformation in motion.

Saxony-Anhalt is also home to the Chemical Triangle around Leuna and Bitterfeld in the eastern part of the state, which still accounts for around 10,000 jobs. To the west lies the Harz mountain range, while the Elbe River, one of Europe's major waterways, flows through the state from southeast to north.

The southern part of Saxony-Anhalt is being forced to reinvent itself as it undergoes structural change following the decision to phase out lignite coal. Unemployment remains slightly above the national average.
How one region in eastern Germany is getting a second chance
Home to around 2.1 million people, it is one of Germany's more sparsely populated states. Only two cities, the state capital Magdeburg and Halle, have more than 200,000 inhabitants.

Nevertheless, in September, international attention is likely to turn to this small eastern German state. For the first time in postwar German history, a candidate from a party that Germany's domestic intelligence agency has classified as "confirmed right-wing extremist" in parts could become the head of a state government. The Alternative for Germany (AfD), whose lead candidate is Ulrich Siegmund, holds a clear lead in all opinion polls.
AfD far ahead in latest polls

Just before the election, the AfD is polling at more than 40% in Saxony-Anhalt. The conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), which has been the dominant governing party in the state since German reunification in 1990, trails far behind, with support ranging between 23% and 26%.

The state office for the protection of the constitution has classified the AfD as a "confirmed right-wing extremist" organization, but this has done little to dent its popularity among voters. The Left Party is polling at 13%, while support for the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) stands at between 6% and 7%. It remains uncertain whether the Greens and the pro-business Free Democratic Party (FDP) will succeed in returning to the state parliament.

CDU politician Reiner Haseloff served as state premier of Saxony-Anhalt for 15 years before stepping down in January 2026. In an interview with Der Spiegel, Haseloff said he had often felt, while sitting in the state parliament in Magdeburg, "as though I were in the final phase of the Weimar Republic's Reichstag, or later in Berlin's Sportpalast."

The Weimar Republic, Germany's first democracy, came to an end in 1933 when the Nazis seized power. It was in Berlin's Sportpalast that Nazi propaganda minister Joseph Goebbels, a close confidant of Adolf Hitler, delivered his notorious 1943 "total war" speech.

Haseloff's successor, Sven Schulze, also of the CDU, must now take on the AfD in the upcoming election. If he fails, the CDU's long dominance of state politics could come to an end. Most recently, the conservatives governed in coalition with the Social Democrats and the FDP.
Saxony-Anhalt's unusual political history

From 1994 to 2002, Saxony-Anhalt was also at the center of national political attention. In July 1994, the Social Democrat Reinhard Höppner formed a minority government with the ecologist Greens that relied on the support of the left-wing Party of Democratic Socialism (PDS), successor to East Germany's ruling Socialist Unity Party.

Just five years after the fall of the Berlin Wall and German reunification, cooperation with the heirs to East Germany's former ruling party was widely seen across the country, especially by conservatives, as crossing a political red line.
What if Germany's far-right AfD party wins in Saxony-Anhalt?

Support for extremist parties has long been stronger in Saxony-Anhalt than in many other parts of Germany. In 1998, the far-right German People's Union (DVU), classified as right-wing extremist, won 12.9% of the vote and entered the state parliament. However, internal divisions within the party were so deep that it chose not to contest the 2002 state election.
What's driving AfD support in Saxony-Anhalt?

Experts attribute the AfD's strong showing in the polls largely to the widespread dissatisfaction many people in the state feel with developments in Germany. Many jobs disappeared in the years following reunification, particularly in the lignite mining and chemical industries.

Saxony-Anhalt also faces pronounced demographic challenges. With an average age of 48.3 years, it had Germany's oldest population in 2024. The state also has a pronounced gender imbalance among younger age groups, with approximately 120,240 men aged 18 to 29 compared with around 103,177 women. At the end of 2025, foreign nationals accounted for about 9% of the population, compared with roughly 15% nationwide. Many young people left the state and never returned.

Many people oppose further immigration, even though the state's foreign population remains comparatively small. Nevertheless, its size has increased markedly over the past decade. According to the state's Statistical Office, the number of people without German citizenship has more than doubled since 2015.
What would AfD rule mean for Saxony-Anhalt?

According to many observers, the success of the far-right DVU some 25 years ago demonstrates that right-wing extremist parties have long had a loyal core electorate in Saxony-Anhalt. Today, that electorate largely backs the AfD, regardless of its election manifesto or policy program.
Threat from the far right: Never quite German enough?

Political scientist Benjamin Höhne of the Chemnitz University of Technology told public broadcaster Deutschlandfunk that he believes the AfD would seek to reshape the constitutional order if it were to take power in Saxony-Anhalt. Liberal democratic and rule-of-law principles, he argued, would be systematically eroded.
"I think the AfD is currently watching the United States very closely," he said. In his view, President Donald Trump's administration in the US is pursuing a similar course.

Höhne believes, however, that such radical agendas would be difficult to implement in a single federal state. "You cannot simply pull a lever in one state and expect everything to fall into line with a far-right script," he said.
One thing seems certain: on September 6, all eyes will be on this small state in the center of Germany.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: Trump hails 'historic' deal for US to control 65bn barrels of Venezuela's oil
articles.summary: Venezuelan interim president says the unusual agreement will help revive her country's economy.

blocks.text: The US has struck a deal with Venezuela to control more than 65 billion barrels of its proven oil reserves, Donald Trump announced.
The US president wrote that the agreement would more than double American oil reserves and "substantially lower Gas Prices for all Americans".
Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodríguez hailed the deal as one that would help her nation's economic revival.
But some analysts have reacted with scepticism, including questioning whether the deal would address long-running obstacles that have deterred investment in Venezuela's oil industry.
Trump has recently been under domestic pressure to tame petrol prices, which have spiked due to the Iran war.
He vowed to tap into Venezuela's reserves, the world's largest, after the US captured its then-President Nicolás Maduro in January, ostensibly to stand trial on drug charges in New York.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the oil deal "a huge win for both the American and Venezuelan people". Few details were released.
"For the Venezuelan people, this deal will bring nearly $100bn (£74bn) in private investment, support thousands of high-paying jobs and drive the reconstruction of Venezuela's economy," he said.
Trump said Rubio and Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth had reached the agreement with Venezuela's leadership "through a partnership with private business".
He did not elaborate on the partnership or describe possible commitments and terms for the US in the deal, but he claimed the agreement was reached "at no cost to the American Taxpayer".
Under the deal the US government will retain 55% control of a joint venture with an "experienced private operator in Venezuela", a US official told the BBC's US partner CBS News.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday that US energy firms Chevron and Halliburton were nearing deals to invest billions in overhauling the infrastructure in Venezuela's oil fields, many of which have not been developed.
David Goldwyn, president of energy consultancy Goldwyn Global Strategies, said there was "no precedent" for the US government entering into a lease to operate Venezuelan oil fields.
It's not clear if such a move would violate Venezuela's constitution or its hydrocarbons law, he told the Reuters news agency.
"It is hard to see how this kind of arrangement would accelerate investment at any material scale," he added, citing Venezuela's political uncertainty, weak power grid, and limited export capacity.
Venezuela's interim president said in a statement that the agreement would have "a significant impact on our nation's revival".

The deal calls for the development of 17 strategic oil fields with a proven potential of 65 billion barrels, as well as "an investment of more than $100bn and more than $209bn in taxes" for Venezuela, Rodríguez said.

"These investments will contribute not only to the recovery and modernisation of our industry, but also to our country's economic growth, the energy security of our hemisphere and greater balance in international markets," she said.
Oil, gas and mineral lawyer Alexander Kuiper told the BBC the deal could be "very significant" but expressed some caution.

"This is definitely a headline to help with oil prices," he said, but added: "What we don't know, is whether or not those reserves turn into actual investment, and how long that investment takes to produce results."

Asked how it would affect oil prices in practice, Kuiper said: "There isn't a switch that you can flip - contracts and agreements have to be put in place... this could take a long time, but it's an important first step."
Delcy Rodríguez - Maduro's former vice-president, who the US backed following his capture - gave the venture a 100-year concession to operate in the oil fields, the unnamed US official told CBS.
Trump gave few specifics of the highly unusual agreement, which apparently grants the US direct governance over a foreign country's sovereign national resources.
The deal would also appear to be wider in scope than the US-led Coalition Provisional Authority's control over Iraq's oil revenues after Saddam Hussein was ousted in an American-led invasion in 2003.

But it is unclear whether the Venezuela agreement could face legal and constitutional challenges in the South American nation. The official text of the agreement between Washington and Caracas has not been published.
Venezuela has the largest proven oil reserves in the world - an estimated 303 billion barrels.
However, production has plummeted since its peak in the late 1990s, in part due to a tightening of controls over its state-run oil firm and US sanctions targeting its main economic lifeline.
Hours after US special forces captured Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, in a raid on the Venezuelan capital, Trump said the US would indefinitely control the sale of the country's oil.

He has also claimed the rights to Venezuela's oil after saying that the country had in the past "unilaterally seized and sold American oil, American assets and American platforms, costing us billions and billions of dollars".

His framing of the deal as part of efforts to drive down domestic petrol prices comes as the global price of oil has jumped up significantly as supply via the Strait of Hormuz in the Persian Gulf has effectively been stymied - spurring discontent ahead of the US midterm elections in November.

However, Venezuela's oil reserves are made up of so-called "heavy, sour" oil, which is harder to refine and used for making diesel and asphalt, while the US typically produces "light, sweet" oil useful for making petrol.
Trump has asked US oil firms to invest at least $100bn (£75bn) to restore the country's oil industry.

articles.title: Cooperatives seek 10-fold tax exemption increase to ₱100 million
articles.summary: The Philippine Chamber of Cooperatives, Inc. (Coop Chamber) is asking Congress to raise the reserve fund tax-exemption ceiling for cooperatives to ₱100 million from the current ₱10 million. Coop…

blocks.text: The Philippine Chamber of Cooperatives, Inc. (Coop Chamber) is asking Congress to raise the reserve fund tax-exemption ceiling for cooperatives to ₱100 million from the current ₱10 million.
Coop Chamber Secretary General Edwin A. Bustillos told reporters that the proposal is a long-overdue update to a four-decade-old threshold, one that will not hurt government coffers.
During technical working group discussions, Bustillos revealed the proposal faced pushback from the Department of Finance (DOF) and the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) over potential revenue losses.
However, Bustillos explained that the ₱10 million threshold was instituted nearly 40 years ago when the sector was significantly smaller.
He noted that surplus funds generated by cooperatives are legally earmarked as statutory reserves for social development rather than commercial profits.

“Cooperatives’ surplus goes back to the people. They have statutory funds that are channeled to the community,” Bustillos said. For instance, roughly ₱3 billion has been injected into community development funds for infrastructure, scholarships, and medical missions, among other initiatives.
Bustillos added that spending on community development, education, and training goes uncounted in gross domestic product (GDP), despite cooperatives pumping billions into these efforts.
The sector also shoulders the cost of leadership training, financial inclusion, and financial literacy programs that would otherwise rely on government agency partnerships.

Furthermore, he stressed that trillions of pesos circulating within the sector help nearly 14 million members start and sustain small businesses, pursue their education, and cover medical bills for family members.

Citing these on-the-ground contributions, the Coop chamber argued that while granting a higher tax relief threshold means forgone tax revenues, those funds ultimately recirculate into local communities.

“Therefore, raising the accumulated reserves threshold to ₱100 million would not result in a significant revenue loss for the BIR and the DOF,” Bustillos said. “Hopefully, the ₱100-million cap will be passed during the Senate’s second regular session.”

Under the Philippine Cooperative Code, registered cooperatives transacting exclusively with members are exempt from national and local internal revenue taxes. Transactions with non-members, however, remain subject to applicable taxes.

Cooperatives with accumulated reserves and undivided net savings of up to ₱10 million enjoy comprehensive tax privileges. Those exceeding the threshold pay taxes on the excess, though they retain specific exemptions for local taxes and qualified transactions.

Bustillos pointed to this framework to clarify that “billionaire” cooperatives still contribute to government revenues by paying taxes on non-member transactions and reserves above the threshold. Only about 140 of the roughly 20,000 cooperatives in the country fall into the “billionaire” category—mostly in finance, with a few in agriculture.
Tax privileges apply only to core activities outlined in their articles of cooperation, bylaws, and BIR tax exemption certificates, leaving all other economic activities taxable.

Beyond tax disputes, the sector is grappling with digital compliance challenges. The Coop Chamber noted that many micro-cooperatives—particularly those representing farmers, fisherfolk, and indigenous peoples—struggle to meet digitized reporting mandates due to a lack of devices and reliable internet access.

To address this, Coop Chamber Chairperson Noel D. Raboy said the group is pushing for compliance relief similar to that offered by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), such as permitting simple bookkeeping instead of requiring costly certified tax accountants (CTAs) for small co-ops.

These ongoing struggles have driven the sector to seek systemic legislative reform. The Coop Chamber plans to consolidate its members into a unified “co-op vote” and field a senatorial candidate under a national cooperative party in the 2028 elections. By placing a cooperative leader in the Senate, the sector aims to champion community-based development and secure lasting policy support for micro-enterprises.

articles.title: When we prettify the cross
articles.summary: THROUGH UNTRUE Imagine if Jesus had lived in our time, preached inconvenient truths, challenged the powerful, and threatened both religious and political authorities. Imagine if He were executed by…
articles.byline: Fr. Rolando V. De La Rosa, OP

blocks.text: THROUGH UNTRUE

Imagine if Jesus had lived in our time, preached inconvenient truths, challenged the powerful, and threatened both religious and political authorities. Imagine if He were executed by electric chair. Would we place electric chairs in our churches instead of crosses?

We may cringe at the thought. But perhaps we react that way because we have prettified the Cross so much that we have forgotten what it originally represented. We now wear necklaces with small crosses as pendants. We adorn church altars and our homes with beautifully crafted crosses. There is nothing wrong with honoring the Cross. But there is a danger in prettifying it that we forget what it actually means.

The Cross was originally an instrument of torture and execution, much like the electric chair. Crucifixion was a public spectacle of extreme suffering and dehumanization. This helps us understand Peter’s reaction when Jesus predicted that He would be crucified. He took Jesus aside and protested: “God forbid! No such thing shall ever happen to you” (Matthew 16:22). Like many Jews of his time, Peter expected the Messiah to be a powerful king, triumphantly wielding authority from His throne, not a helpless man hanging on a cross.

We are not so different from Peter. We adore Christ crucified, but a prettified Cross can become just an ornament, that is beautiful to behold, but demanding little from us. It reflects our preference for a God who gives us everything but asks nothing in return.

The philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche criticized Christianity for glorifying weakness and suffering. From his perspective, venerating the Cross could seem like celebrating the plight of those crushed or victimized by human cruelty. But perhaps Nietzsche’s mistake was to assume that power must always express itself through domination and self-will. What if God reveals a different kind of power, a power that does not crush the weak but joins them in their suffering? What if the Cross demonstrates His refusal to abandon us in our darkest moments?

On the Cross, Jesus revealed that God does not love us from a distance. He is not indifferent to the pain that afflicts us. He comes close to us and embraces our suffering so that, ultimately, He can overcome it through love. Unbelievers may see only a man hanging on a cross, but we Christians see God hanging there, revealing the depth of His unconditional love for us.

The Cross tells us what love looks like when it refuses to surrender, run away, or give up. That is why Jesus’ words in today’s Gospel are addressed not only to His first disciples but to all of us: “Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me. For whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for me will find it” (Matthew 16:24–25).

So, when you look at a cross today, or when you touch the cross hanging around your neck, listen to the uncomfortable questions it asks you: What are you willing to sacrifice for the love of God? And perhaps the most difficult question of all: Can you remain faithful to God when He seems to have abandoned you?

On the cross, Jesus cried out, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46). Yet He did not turn away from the Father. That is why the cross is not merely a symbol of suffering. It is the ultimate sign of faith that endures when God seems silent and absent.

I once presided at the funeral Mass of a man who had achieved much in his lifetime, only to undergo a terrible ordeal because of a terminal illness. In her eulogy, his daughter said: “We have great love and respect for our father. But we admire him most, not for his success and achievements, but for the way he embraced the intolerable pain he had to endure every day. It was when he became most helpless that he showed us what courage truly means. He bravely clung to his faith despite the excruciating pain he had to bear. Perhaps this is the greatest legacy he has left us, his children.”

articles.title: A week of initialisms and acronyms
articles.summary: While most will refer to both categories as acronyms; initialisms are read letter by letter, while acronyms are a short word made from the letters of a long group of words. For today’s column, the…

blocks.text: While most will refer to both categories as acronyms; initialisms are read letter by letter, while acronyms are a short word made from the letters of a long group of words. For today’s column, the initialisms would be DTI for Department of Trade and Industry, and AI for Artificial Intelligence; while the acronym for Artist Atelier Philippines, would be the newly coined ARTa. Here are two launch events I recently had the pleasure of attending.

blocks.caption: Dennis Uy of Converge ICT Solutions, Inc, DTI Sec. Cristina Roque, and Dindo Marzan of the SME Group; at the DTI AI and Scale Up Center.

blocks.text: Dennis Uy of Converge ICT Solutions, Inc, DTI Sec. Cristina Roque, and Dindo Marzan of the SME Group; at the DTI AI and Scale Up Center.

The DTI AI and Scale Up Center - Our Department of Trade and Industry, in partnership with Converge ICT Solutions, launched the DTI AI and Scale Up Center at their Gil Puyat office. It’s a practical hub for technology adoption and potential business growth. At its core, it’s a hands on resource facility; that allows companies, start-ups, and local SMEs to learn how to integrate AI and digital tools into their operations. Backed by the Tatak Pinoy Strategy, the Philippine Innovation Act, and the Innovative Start Up Act, I really appreciated the intent of what was being officially opened that afternoon.

It’s no longer just words on official documents or lofty aims of an existing Strategy and Acts; but the realization of that intent, and establishing concrete avenues to achieve those goals. Too often, we speak of Philippine businesses not being competitive in the global market, or that we lag behind in incorporating technology, or that we find scaling up to be too formidable a task. Here then was the DTI taking the proverbial bull by the horns, and creating a solution-based pathway.

As DTI Secretary Cristina Roque was proud to say, “This AI and Scale Up Center provides a realistic, accessible entry point for Filipino businesses to explore and adapt modern technology like AI. Scaling a business requires usable tools and expert guidance, so that innovative ideas can turn into functional solutions. By bringing technology leaders like Converge together with our local enterprises, we are giving businesses of all sizes the practical knowledge and connectivity they need to improve efficiency, and stay competitive.”

blocks.caption: Catz Jalandoni, DTI Sec. Cristina Roque, Margarita Delgado, and Karen Davila, at the DTI.

blocks.text: Catz Jalandoni, DTI Sec. Cristina Roque, Margarita Delgado, and Karen Davila, at the DTI.

From Practical Workshops, to technical consultations, and scaling programs; Converge is ready to be that ideal partner in making these all available to our SMEs. As Converge founder and CEO Dennis Uy remarked, “We are proud to partner with DTI in helping local businesses take realistic steps toward digital transformation. Through reliable connectivity and hands on technology solutions, our goal is to help companies understand AI, streamline their operations, and expand their reach in today’s evolving market.”

With the array of DTI’s private sector partners who were on hand to show their support; the know how, technical expertise, and best practices learned by other established local businesses will be made available for our SMEs to learn from, as made accessible and powered by Converge.

I salute this partnership, and the Center that has been created; and can only hope that SMEs will appreciate the great opportunity being offered, and how it’s a ‘helping hand’ that can go a very long way.

blocks.caption: The Management and Faculty at ARTa (Artist Atelier Philippines).

blocks.text: The Management and Faculty at ARTa (Artist Atelier Philippines).

ARTa, the Artist Atelier Philippines - There’s a new Creative Learning Center that’s located at the Kirov Tower, Proscenium, Rockwell Center, Makati; and it’s the brainchild of noted businesswoman and artist Elena Coyiuto. For those familiar with Elena and her IG handle madameinshades, they’ll acknowledge that her readiness to support worthy causes is matched by her vitality and dedication to the Arts. Having mounted solo exhibits of her own paintings, it would only be a logical extension to want to share the wonders of this mid-life shift; and offer it to others who may also be yearning to express themselves in a medium they have had no training for.

And that’s precisely what the Artist Atelier Philippines (ARTa) hopes to provide. In the atelier’s curriculum are visual and literary arts programs for beginners, for hobbyists, and the aspiring artist. It’s guided instruction that may help answer one’s perpetual wondering if there was some form of artistic expression that one can rekindle or simply ignite. It’s the “What If…” being given that window of opportunity to become a reality. It may be what Elena herself faced at one point in her journey; and she’s evidently saying that if one needs help in navigating, she’s offering a wonderful option.

blocks.caption: Elena Coyiuto, at her new advocacy - a creative space called ARTa (from her IG page.)

blocks.text: Elena Coyiuto, at her new advocacy - a creative space called ARTa (from her IG page.)

From Drawing, to Acrylic Painting, Watercolor, Creative Writing, and even such specialized subjects as Floral Arranging, and Weaving, ARTa is offering basic and intermediate programs. No portfolio required, the courses are accessible to all. One can even arrange for private group sessions, and corporate workshops.

Elena Coyiuto remarked, “ARTa is my advocacy in sharing the love of art and making creativity accessible to everyone. I hope to inspire people of all ages and skill levels to explore their creativity and discover art as a lifelong source of expression, connection, and personal growth.” Head to the ARTa Philippines website, or check their IG and FB pages.

articles.title: Mass transport that works: Fulfilling the promise of the EDSA Busway
articles.summary: ENDEAVOR During the Covid-19 pandemic, the Department of Transportation (DOTr) led by then Secretary Arthur “Art” Tugade took the initiative of launching the EDSA Busway or EDSA Carousel project in…

blocks.text: ENDEAVOR

During the Covid-19 pandemic, the Department of Transportation (DOTr) led by then Secretary Arthur “Art” Tugade took the initiative of launching the EDSA Busway or EDSA Carousel project in June 2020 to ease the daily commute problems of tens of thousands of Filipinos. Within a month, a dedicated median us lane adjacent to the MRT-3 line had been installed.

Moreover, the DOTr rationalized the operations of public utility buses. Sixty-one fragmented feeder routes were replaced with a single, streamlined Carousel route running from Monumento in Caloocan down to the Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX).

Concrete barriers were installed for physical segregation from general traffic and special buses with left-facing doors were introduced. A public-private partnership agreement was forged with the SM Group to build elevated median stations and pedestrian concourses. These structures directly link major commercial hubs to the inner-lane EDSA Carousel stations, namely: SM North EDSA in Quezon City; SM Megamall (Mandaluyong and Ortigas); and SM Mall of Asia in Pasay City. The SM Group donated commercial spaces and assumed full funding for the construction of three major state-of-the-art concourses in the three mall sites.

Under the agreement, SM secured the rights to name the stations, administer, maintain, and manage the facilities based on DOTr guidelines. This arrangement ensured long-term, high-quality upkeep and security for the pedestrian hubs
The concourses were designed based on the conceptual framework of urban transport reform advocate Eduardo Yap.

Despite policy support, advocacy groups like the Move as One Coalition have flagged zero funding allocated specifically for the EDSA Busway under the DOTr's proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP). The DOTr defends this fiscal shift by leaning into the aforementioned public-private partnership (PPP) model to sustain future upgrades while keeping current systems rolling.

Recall that the EDSA Busway emerged as a model implementation of the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) framework established by the PPP Center under the stewardship of Cosette Canilao during the Aquino administration. Ms. Canilao has since joined Aboitiz InfraCapital, the infrastructure investment arm of the Aboitiz Group, as President and CEO.
For the sake of long-term infrastructure development, it is imperative to adopt a proactive and decisive stance in implementing the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) template.

The executive branch must demonstrate its political will in completing priority infrastructure projects like the EDSA Busway. Prolonged pauses will be detrimental rather than helpful, as time is ticking away. There are only less than two years before the expiry of the current administration’s watch and it stands to reason that it would like to be remembered as a regime that responded to urgent concerns of the citizenry just like the easing of mobility throughout the EDSA corridor.

High hopes were ignited when Vince Dizon was appointed as transportation secretary, but his stint was short-lived. Even before completing nine months at its helm, he was called to take over the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to stem the tide of the public outrage over ghost flood control projects.

The EDSA Busway has already demonstrated a simple but powerful truth. When government gives priority to public transportation, millions of commuters stand to benefit. What began as an emergency response to the pandemic has evolved into a vital component of Metro Manila’s mass transport system. The challenge now is to finish what has been started and to do it expeditiously.

SM Prime Holdings’ commitment to complete three major EDSA Busway stations should be welcomed as an example of the efficacy of the PPP approach. Properly designed and completed, they will make the Busway a showcase of safer, more accessible and more convenient commuting, particularly for senior citizens, persons with disabilities, women, children and daily commuters bearing the brunt of long journeys that take many hours to complete, thereby sapping huge stores of energy and reducing quality time for families.

Government must move with dispatch and determination, establishing clear timelines for completion and operationalization. When a public transport solution works, government should not allow it to languish. It should make it better, expand its reach and finish the job.

Once completed, the EDSA Busway will demonstrate with clarity that government is capable of bringing to full fruition effective solutions that give to the people what they have always longed to attain: safe and dignified travel and a better quality of daily life.

articles.title: The paradox of the cross
articles.summary: REFLECTIONS TODAY It is often said that the Christian faith took the whole Mediterranean world by storm; what started as an insignificant “Jesus movement” in Palestine soon became a universal…

blocks.text: REFLECTIONS TODAY

It is often said that the Christian faith took the whole Mediterranean world by storm; what started as an insignificant “Jesus movement” in Palestine soon became a universal religion that encompassed the whole Roman Empire. St. Luke who narrates the development and spread of Christianity in Acts of the Apostles provides the explanation through a word of caution of Rabbi Gamaliel to the Sanhedrin concerning the intransigent Apostles: “Have nothing to do with these men, and let them go. For if this endeavor or this activity is of human origin, it will destroy itself. But if it comes from God, you will not be able to destroy them; you may even find yourselves fighting against God” (Acts 5:38-39). That finally Paul the Apostle arrives in Rome, in chains and yet free to preach the Gospel, proves this: the nascent faith-movement comes from God and human beings cannot destroy it.

Being of divine origin does not mean, however, that Christianity triumphed mightily over the ancient religions like Gideon dispersing the Midianite army with blowing of horns and breaking of jars (Jgs 7:20) or Joshua causing the walls of Jericho to collapse with a seven-day march around the city (Jos 6:4). Christianity conquered the hearts of peoples with what St. Paul calls “the message of the cross”—foolishness to the pagans and a stumbling block to Jews, but to the believers, the power and the wisdom of God (1 Cor 1:22-24).

In today’s Gospel, Simon Peter is shocked to hear Jesus predicting that he will suffer and die in Jerusalem. And rightly so! He had just confessed Jesus as the Messiah of God, and Jesus had called him “Rock” because of that confession. How, then, can Jesus speak of the cross when a crucified man is cursed by God! The Messiah was thought to be a glorious figure, not a man of suffering! The message is just as shocking when preached to the Gentile world. A crucified Messiah as God’s means of reconciling a lost world was a bizarre message, not “good news.” In the early third century, the pagan Caecilius Natalis said of the Christians, “I hear that they adore the head of an ass, the basest of creatures—a most worthy and appropriate religion for such manners.” A graffito of a man’s body with an ass’s head found in Palestine reflects a similar response by Gentiles to the “folly of the cross.” Under this graffito was the caption: “Alexamenos worships [his] God.”

The cross can only be “good news” if its meaning is completely overturned. This was shown in the resurrection of Jesus. God was pleased with the obedience “unto death, unto the cross” of Jesus that he raised him from the dead. St. Paul, the first theologian, was a theologian of the cross. According to him, the cross is the initiative of God and the demonstration of his great love: “God proves his love for us in that while we were still sinners Christ died for us” (Rom 5:8). Jesus’ cross is not an accident of history but a historical witness of God’s unmerited love and saving grace: God was reconciling the world to himself through Christ (cf 2 Cor 5:19).

Paul came to this realization not as an afterthought but through a dramatic encounter with the risen Christ. On the way to Damascus, Christ “apprehended” him and showed him that he is in fact what the disciples preached him to be. Paul was struck by the “power and glory of the cross” as if by lightning.
This was the conviction that he then preached to both Jews and Gentiles. They understood the paradox of the cross and became believers, ready to lose their lives that they might find it in Jesus.
First Reading • Jer 20:7-9
You duped me, O Lord, and I let myself be duped; you were too strong for me, and you triumphed. All the day I am an object of laughter; everyone mocks me.
Whenever I speak, I must cry out, violence and outrage is my message; the word of the Lord has brought me derision and reproach all the day.
I say to myself, I will not mention him, I will speak in his name no more. But then it becomes like fire burning in my heart, imprisoned in my bones; I grow weary holding it in, I cannot endure it.
Source: “365 Days with the Lord 2026,” St. Paul’s, 7708 St. Paul Rd., SAV, Makati City (Phils.); Tel.: 632-895-9701; E-mail: [email protected]; Website: http://www.stpauls.ph.

articles.title: Lubao flooding exposes urgent need for better flood control
articles.summary: A two-storey house being swallowed by a raging river should never be dismissed as just another dramatic video content. But that was precisely what happened in Barangay Sta. Rita-Sto. Cristo, Lubao,…

blocks.text: A two-storey house being swallowed by a raging river should never be dismissed as just another dramatic video content.

But that was precisely what happened in Barangay Sta. Rita-Sto. Cristo, Lubao, Pampanga, on Aug. 28. As floodwaters surged, the riverbank gave way and a home was swept into the torrent and then swallowed by the rampaging floodwater in a matter of minutes. The terrifying and heart-wrenching scene is a warning—and an indictment of how dangerously unprepared communities remain for extreme flooding.

The timing could hardly be more ominous. On Aug. 29, PAGASA placed Pampanga and neighboring provinces under a red rainfall warning as the southwest monsoon, or habagat, continued to dump heavy rain over parts of Luzon. A red warning means serious flooding is expected in flood-prone areas.
The Sta. Rita Dam incident exposes a problem far bigger than one overwhelmed structure.

The National Irrigation Administration said a huge volume of water rushed downstream and overwhelmed the dam, while debris from forests and agricultural areas accumulated and clogged some of its gates. The resulting surge damaged portions of the slope protection and retaining wall.
That demands accountability. But accountability must be comprehensive.

The government must answer for whether dams, dikes, drainage systems, and flood-control structures are properly designed, maintained, inspected and upgraded. It must explain whether danger zones are being enforced and why residential structures continue to exist along vulnerable riverbanks and dikes.
But the government is not the only actor responsible.

Illegal logging and destructive land-clearing practices, including kaingin in vulnerable upland areas, must be confronted because denuded watersheds can worsen erosion and send enormous amounts of debris downstream. If investigations establish that illegally cut timber or other improperly managed upland debris contributed to the obstruction at Sta. Rita, those responsible must be held accountable.
Residents, too, must face the truth, unforgettable as it may be: Like them, a river needs space to avoid swelling.

Building houses on dikes, easements, and riverbanks may appear harmless when the river is calm. During extreme rainfall, however, such structures can endanger lives—and serve as obstacles that complicate flood management and evacuation.
The answer is not another round of promises after disaster strikes.

The government must pursue integrated flood mitigation: Rehabilitate watersheds, enforce river easements, clear waterways and drainage channels before the rainy season, modernize dams and dikes, strengthen flood forecasting and early-warning systems, and conduct regular independent safety audits of critical infrastructure. Flood-control projects must also be transparent, scientifically designed, and subjected to public scrutiny.

The private sector must do its share. Developers must respect hazard maps and no-build zones. Industries must prevent waste and debris from entering waterways. Companies can finance watershed rehabilitation, river cleanup, community early-warning systems and disaster-preparedness programs—not merely distribute relief goods after floods.
And every Filipino has a responsibility.

Do not dump garbage into waterways. Do not build illegally on riverbanks and dikes. Report illegal logging, destructive land clearing, and unsafe construction. Heed evacuation orders. Participate in community disaster-preparedness efforts. Most importantly, demand accountability for every peso spent on flood-control infrastructure.
Climate and extreme weather may be beyond anyone’s control. But negligence is not.

The house swept away in Lubao should therefore become a national lesson. Flooding is not simply a natural disaster. Its consequences are shaped by decisions made in government offices, boardrooms, forests, farms, construction sites, and communities.
The Lubao river has delivered its warning.
Now the country must decide whether to listen, or wait for the next structure to disappear.

articles.title: Artemis II astronauts receive nation's highest space honor for their successful moonshot
articles.summary:
Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen received the Congressional Space Medal of Honor

The Artemis II…

blocks.text: The Artemis II astronauts who flew around the moon in April received the US’s highest space honor on Friday.
Donald Trump presented the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to the three Americans and one Canadian whose lunar flyby for the US space agency Nasa set a new distance record for humanity.

Nasa’s administrator, Jared Isaacman, and other dignitaries took part in the packed ceremony at Houston’s Johnson Space Center, home to mission control. The president used the occasion to announce the creation of a US space academy for the nation’s space force as well as Nasa and the commercial space community.
“Space is the hot thing,” Trump told the crowd, adding that the academy’s location has yet to be determined.

Cmdr Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, and mission specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen, a Canadian, became the first astronauts to travel to the moon in more than half a century, coming within 4,067 miles (6,545km) while test-driving Nasa’s new Orion capsule. They were the first to launch onboard Nasa’s new moon rocket, a 30-story behemoth that had soared only once before from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center.

While they didn’t stop at the moon, the four set the stage for next year’s Artemis III docking rehearsal in orbit around Earth. Artemis IV’s moon landing by two astronauts, near the lunar south pole, could follow as soon as 2028.
Trump said Americans will land back on the moon before his second presidency ends. Mars is next – “very shortly”, he said.
The president called the newest recipients “four intrepid space heroes”. He pointed out that they did not do it alone, thanking all who contributed to the Artemis II mission.
“There are no finer humans we could have sent as our ambassadors to the stars,” Isaacman added.

Wiseman and his crew are in good company, with only 30 astronauts receiving the prestigious honor before them. Many of the recipients were honored posthumously following their spaceflight-related deaths.

Apollo 11 commander Neil Armstrong – whose phrase “that’s one step for man, one giant leap for mankind” gripped the world when he became the first person to walk on the moon on 20 July 1969 – was the first to receive the Congressional Space Medal of Honor.

President Jimmy Carter awarded six of these medals in 1978, which also went to Alan Shepard, the first American in space; John Glenn, the first American in orbit; and Apollo 8 commander Frank Borman, whose 1968 mission marked humanity’s first lunar voyage.

The most recent recipients were Doug Hurley and Bob Behnken, the first astronauts to launch aboard a SpaceX rocket. Coming nine years after the space shuttle program’s close, their 2020 test flight to the International Space Station restored the US’s ability to launch crews from home soil. Joe Biden awarded them the medals in 2023, during the third year of his presidency.
Dozens of astronauts participated in the ceremony, including Apollo 17 moonwalker Harrison Schmitt, who is now 91 – and the four men assigned to Nasa’s upcoming Artemis III mission.
Schmitt noted that his mission – Apollo’s last moonshot – was the most productive lunar exploration yet.
“Soon to be surpassed by Artemis,” he said of active astronauts standing behind him.

Nasa plans a sustainable moon base staffed by astronauts and robots near the lunar south pole, where permanently shadowed craters are thought to hold tons of frozen water that could be turned into rocket fuel and drinking water. China is eyeing the same region.
“The second space race has begun,” Nasa’s deputy administrator, Matthew Anderson, said.

As the two-hour ceremony came to a close, the Artemis II astronauts presented Trump with his own blue flight jacket complete with space patches, which they had promised him while visiting him in the Oval Office after their mission.

The president then hustled over to mission control to call the three US astronauts onboard the International Space Station. He informed them of the new US space academy, then briefly handed the phone to two of their spouses for a quick hello.

articles.title: Vehicles swept down collapsed Agana Bridge; one person rescued
articles.summary: TARLAC CITY — Rescue teams continued their search Saturday night for possible victims after vehicles were reportedly swept down following the collapse of the Agana Bridge amid persistent heavy rains…

blocks.text: TARLAC CITY — Rescue teams continued their search Saturday night for possible victims after vehicles were reportedly swept down following the collapse of the Agana Bridge amid persistent heavy rains and strong currents in the Tarlac River.
Authorities confirmed that one survivor was rescued and brought to the Tarlac Provincial Hospital for medical assessment.
The City government of Tarlac said, the search and rescue operations remain ongoing .
Responders were still checking the area for other possible victims to determine the full extent of the incident.
The Agana Bridge has been closed to all motorists following damage attributed to continuous rainfall and the strong flow of water in the Tarlac River.
Authorities have warned motorists and residents not to attempt to cross or pass through the damaged bridge, citing the continuing danger in the area.
Motorists were already advised to take alternative routes and closely follow instructions from authorities .
Rescue and emergency operations are underway.
Residents in nearby and low-lying areas were likewise urged to remain vigilant, as rains continue to affect parts of Tarlac.
Emergency response teams remain on standby.
Related Tags

articles.title: Ombudsman questions bail for convicted officials
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla has questioned the courts’ decision to grant bail to individuals while their convictions are under appeal, saying convicted government officials should start…

blocks.text: Building of the Office of the Ombudsman.
Ombudsman office via FB

MANILA, Philippines — Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla has questioned the courts’ decision to grant bail to individuals while their convictions are under appeal, saying convicted government officials should start serving their sentences immediately.
Remulla criticized how the Sandiganbayan has convicted and imposed sentences on erring government officials but only a few were imprisoned.

“Once convicted by the Sandiganbayan or a lower court for graft, you go to jail. But the courts are being too kind. Instead, they grant bail,” Remulla said during his radio show Executive Session on dzRH.
He also criticized the low amount of bail usually set by the court, proposing that it should be equivalent to “the cost of damage” committed by the convicted official.
Remulla said his office will look at the list of officials who have been convicted by the Sandiganbayan to check whether they are in prison or not.
The ombudsman also pointed out how some cases take a long time to be resolved, with some spanning for 15 years, particularly in resolving appeals.
He said there should be stricter requirements and a deadline for resolving appeals so that the convicted individual is not set free indefinitely.
“The problem is once a motion for reconsideration is filed, a bail is granted with no deadline. Will they sit on that forever?” Remulla pointed out.
He urged the Supreme Court to police the judiciary and called on the public to keep watch on the duties of both the ombudsman and the judiciary.
“I urge members of the judiciary to do their jobs,” he said.

articles.title: Lacson claims proof of illegally reclaimed Taguig land
articles.summary: Sen. Panfilo Lacson said he has identified four parcels of illegally reclaimed land in Taguig using “fraudulently” issued land titles, while at least four other parcels have allegedly no…

blocks.text: Sen. Panfilo Lacson on February 10, 2026.
STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Panfilo Lacson said he has identified four parcels of illegally reclaimed land in Taguig using “fraudulently” issued land titles, while at least four other parcels have allegedly no plotted title lots in the digital file of the Land Registration Authority (LRA).
Lacson tweeted the details of the alleged fraudulent land titles in Taguig’s lakeshore development to dispel Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano’s dismissal of the allegations as false.

“Since Sen. Cayetano keeps publicly asking for evidence, I’ll give it to him, in the spirit of public interest,” Lacson posted on X. He was reacting to Cayetano’s Facebook Live on Thursday, where the Minority Leader said he is “hurt” for the 1.3 million residents of Taguig because Lacson is spreading “fake news” about the city.

Lacson said the details of the four “fraudulently” titled parcels involve one covered by an Administrative Patent, involving 9,204 square meters under an Original Certificate of Title; one covered through Judicial/Ordinary Land Registration Processing covering an area of 5,000 square meters under an OCT; one covered by a Homestead Patent involving 181,077 square meters under a Transfer Certificate of Title and one involving 193,027 square meters under a TCT.
Lacson withheld details like the names of those to whom the titles were issued, as well as the OCT and TCT numbers, with the investigation still ongoing.
These will be turned over to the ombudsman as part of its fact-finding probe on Taguig’s allegedly anomalous lakeshore development and reclamation in the guise of flood control and slope protection.
Lacson earlier said the LRA is digging up details on land titles covering some 38.83 hectares of illegally reclaimed areas on the Taguig side of Laguna Lake.
The uncovered land titles were based on the materials provided by the Philippine Reclamation Authority to Lacson’s office.

articles.title: Cardinal laments flooding despite billions already spent
articles.summary: The country is facing an absurd situation where some of the most heavily flooded communities are also places where billions have supposedly been spent for controversial flood control projects,…

blocks.text: Bishop Pablo Virgilio David of Kalookan, president of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of the Philippines.
Interaksyon / CBCP News

MANILA, Philippines — The country is facing an absurd situation where some of the most heavily flooded communities are also places where billions have supposedly been spent for controversial flood control projects, Kalookan Bishop Pablo Virgilio Cardinal David said yesterday.

“Now imagine having to spend billions more – not to build new infrastructure, but to demolish or correct flood control structures that should never have been built that way in the first place,” David said on Facebook.
He made the statement amid the flooding experienced in many areas in the country.

“Citizens of this country, let us unite. We have nothing to lose but our misery. Go to bisto.ph and join the citizens’ ground validation of government infrastructure projects. Register as a volunteer,” David said.

“Take photographs. Document what you see. If possible, bring engineers, architects, environmental planners or other knowledgeable citizens who can help assess the work. Submit your findings to the Bisto Proyekto advocacy initiative,” he added.
He said “let the evidence lead to investigation, prosecution and accountability.”
David added that the country cannot solve an ecological problem merely by pouring more concrete.

“We have to restore watersheds, protect rivers and wetlands, manage our waste, plan our cities intelligently, prepare for rising seas and a changing climate – and make every infrastructure project part of a coherent, science-based master plan,” he said.
Meanwhile, Antipolo Bishop Ruperto Cruz Santos prayed for protection and peace amid rains brought by the southwest monsoon.

“Livelihoods have been washed away, families displaced, homes destroyed and entire neighborhoods submerged. Lord, look with mercy upon Your people. We beg You: stretch out Your mighty hand and calm the rains. Hold back the floods. Strengthen the land. Protect our communities. Guard every family, every child, every worker, every rescuer and every soul caught in danger,” Santos prayed.

articles.title: Over P5 billion needed to rebuild storm-hit classrooms
articles.summary: At least P5.072 billion is needed for the reconstruction of 476 schools damaged by the southwest monsoon and recent tropical cyclones, the Department of Education said yesterday in a situation report.

blocks.text: Meanwhile, at least P1.013 billion is needed to fund the major repair of 624 schools, the DepEd Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Service said.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — At least P5.072 billion is needed for the reconstruction of 476 schools damaged by the southwest monsoon and recent tropical cyclones, the Department of Education (DepEd) said yesterday in a situation report.
No less than P277.34 million will also be needed for the minor repair of 1,444 schools and another P46.983 million for the cleanup and clearing operations of another 1,627.
The DepEd said that 1,145 classrooms in 307 schools are still being used as evacuation centers for at least 9,798 families.

These include 172 evacuation centers in Central Luzon; 57 evacuation centers in Calabarzon; 37 evacuation centers in Ilocos Region; 15 evacuation centers in Metro Manila; 11 evacuation centers in Eastern Visayas; eight evacuation centers in Mimaropa and seven evacuation centers in the Cordillera Administrative Region.

“The Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Service maintains close coordination with field offices to track emerging impacts, validate class suspension data through the ‘Walang Pasok’ monitor and support timely clearing and repair of affected schools,” DepEd said.

DepEd advised field offices and school disaster risk reduction and management teams to sustain monitoring and operational readiness as weather conditions remain capable of triggering localized flooding, landslides and further disruptions.

articles.title: Sara lawyer doubts Madriaga will be presented as witness
articles.summary: A lawyer for Vice President Sara Duterte said the prosecution will not present alleged bagman Ramil Madriaga as witness in the ongoing impeachment trial.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A lawyer for Vice President Sara Duterte said the prosecution will not present alleged bagman Ramil Madriaga as witness in the ongoing impeachment trial.
In an interview with Bilyonaryo News Channel, Paolo Panelo – counsel of Duterte in the perjury complaint filed against Madriaga before the Taguig Prosecutor’s Office – cited his credibility.
“To me, the prosecution will not present (Madriaga as witness). On the part of the defense, I would not know,” Panelo said.
Duterte filed two perjury cases against Madriaga.
The second perjury complaint was based on Madriaga’s supplemental affidavit, where he claimed to have served as the Vice President’s “bagman.”

Duterte’s first perjury complaint against Madriaga stemmed from the latter’s claim that drug lords and Chinese-sponsored Philippine offshore gaming operators bankrolled her campaign for vice president.
“This is a confession that even the prosecution doesn’t believe in Madriaga anymore,” Panelo added.
He said once the prosecution presents Madriaga during the impeachment trial, the defense would prove that he is lying during the cross-examination.
“So, either way, for me, using Ramil Madriaga here in the impeachment trial would benefit VP Sara and would not benefit those who are criticizing her,” Panelo said.
Panelo described Madriaga as a Trojan Horse.
“That’s why we’re holding interviews, media engagements so I can share the contents of our perjury complaint to show that this witness has no credibility,” he said.
‘Not part of’ defense team

“The truth of the matter is Mr. Madriaga is listed as a witness in the prosecution according to their pre-trial brief. He’s also listed as our witness in our pre-trial brief. But see, Atty. Panelo is not part of the defense team,” defense spokesman Michael Poa said.

Poa issued the reaction after Panelo said Madriaga could be a Trojan Horse for the defense even if he lied when he read his sworn supplemental affidavit during the hearing of the House committee on justice on April 14, claiming that Duterte’s P125-million confidential funds were spent in less than 24 hours and not 11 days as previously reported.

articles.title: Barbers offers compromise, seeks leniency on sub judice ruling
articles.summary: Fully aware of what's at stake, House impeachment adviser Robert Ace Barbers has sought leniency from the Senate impeachment court as far as the sub judice rule in Vice President Sara Duterte's trial…

blocks.text: Fully aware of what's at stake, House impeachment adviser Robert Ace Barbers has sought leniency from the Senate impeachment court as far as the sub judice rule in Vice President Sara Duterte's trial is concerned.
According to Barbers, the court must observe flexibility in order to help the public understand the high-stake proceedings.

“Personally ako, ang aking apela ay magkaroon ng leniency. Payagan ang ating ibang mga prosecutors as long as hindi sila magdi-discuss ng merito na makakapag-influence sa desisyon na maaaring gawin ng ating mga senator-judges,” he said on Aug. 29 during the the Saturday News Forum in Quezon City.
(Personally, my appeal is for leniency. Let our other prosecutors speak as long as they do not discuss the merits in a way that could influence the decision that our senator-judges may make.)
Presiding officer Senator Francis "Chiz" Escudero recently made a ruling that essentially prohibited parties from discussing merits of the trial outside the court.
With this, lawyers from the prosecution and defense panels could no longer or join press conferences.

Escudero's ruling prohibits public comments on disputed facts, witness credibility, the weight or sufficiency of evidence, the legal viability of a charge or defense, and the possible outcome of the trial.

But Barbers sees a possible compromise: he said prosecutors could, for instance, relay statements already made by witnesses in open court without commenting on their credibility or the weight of their testimony.
Barbers said some latitude could be considered given the sui generis, or unique, nature of impeachment proceedings and the public interest in understanding the trial.
“Sabi nga, itong impeachment ay sui generis. Baka sakaling pwedeng medyo luwag-luwagan natin dahil ang pinaka-objective sana ay ma-inform ang publiko kung ano iyong totoong nangyayari,” he said.
(As they say, this impeachment is sui generis. Perhaps we can be a little more lenient because the main objective should be to inform the public about what is really happening.)
He stressed the importance of helping Filipinos understand the impeachment process and what transpires during the trial.
Barbers said designated spokespersons for both the prosecution and defense could provide accurate information while helping counter misinformation.

“Itong pag-a-appoint ng mga designated spokespersons sa bawat panig, iyong defense at iyong prosecution, ay para magkaroon ng tama, accurate, at hindi fake news na mga impormasyon sa labas ng ating korte,” he said.

(The appointment of designated spokespersons for each side, the defense and the prosecution, is intended to ensure that the public receives correct, accurate, and non-fake-news information outside our court.)
His appeal notwithstanding, the former House quad-committee (quad-comm) overall chairman stressed that the prosecution team would comply with the court’s ruling.
Barbers also maintained that the sub judice restrictions should be applied uniformly to everyone covered by the ruling, including senator-judges.

articles.title: Beyond the beaches: The story Panglao tells through Hudyaka Festival 2026
articles.summary: PANGLAO, BOHOL, Philippines — The streets of this tourist town came alive on Friday, Aug. 28, as 10 barangays showcased their culture, traditions and faith through the Hudyaka sa Panglao Festival…

blocks.text: PANGLAO, BOHOL, Philippines — The streets of this tourist town came alive on Friday, Aug. 28, as 10 barangays showcased their culture, traditions and faith through the Hudyaka sa Panglao Festival 2026.

Known as a major tourism destination in Bohol, Panglao is famous for its white-sand beaches, clear waters and dive sites. But during the annual festival, residents showed that the town’s attractions go beyond its natural wonders.
The festival’s main events—the street dancing and ritual showdown—featured performances inspired by the history, livelihood, food and communities of Panglao.
The contingents highlighted stories from their respective barangays, including fishing, tuba gathering, local products and tourist destinations.

Barangay Poblacion paid tribute to pan pati, a popular local bread, through its performance. The presentation honored the people who started making the bread and the generations that kept the tradition alive.

Barangay Danao, meanwhile, presented a story of perseverance through a working student who finished his studies, found a job and eventually fulfilled his dream of providing a home for his father, with faith in St. Augustine playing an important role in his journey.
The performances drew residents, tourists and expatriates who lined the streets to watch the colorful costumes, elaborate props and synchronized dances accompanied by drums and native gongs.
Danao won the street dancing competition, followed by Bil-isan in second place and Poblacion in third.

Poblacion won the ritual showdown, with Bil-isan placing second and Danao third. Poblacion also received Best in Choreography and Best in Costumes. Tangnan won Best in Andas (processional carriage), while Danao received Best in Musicality.

blocks.caption: Performers bring energy, color, and rhythm to the Hudyaka sa Panglao 2026 Street Dancing Competition on Friday, August 28, in Panglao town, Bohol.

blocks.text: For 17-year-old Poblacion performer Gwenn Balbiran, the weeks of nightly rehearsals were worth the effort.
“We offer our dance to Saint Augustine, and for our love of Panglao,” she said.
Kyla Tiempo, 20, another Poblacion dancer, said their performance was an expression of their faith.
“This is our devotion to God and our patron Saint Augustine,” she said.
Rooted in faith
Hudyaka sa Panglao, which means merrymaking in Cebuano, was first held in 1987 as part of the town’s annual fiesta in honor of St. Augustine of Hippo. It is the oldest festival in the province.
According to co-founder Rosario Estoquia, the festival has continued to grow each year, becoming bigger and more colorful while maintaining its connection to the community.
The celebration was held online in 2020 and 2021 because of the COVID-19 pandemic. It returned to the streets in 2022.
Panglao’s contingent has also competed in the Sinulog Festival in Cebu, where it won a competition.
Mayor Edgardo Arcay said Hudyaka helps strengthen unity among residents while promoting Panglao as a tourist destination.
“This festival is about celebrating who we are as Panglaonons—our culture, our heritage, our devotion, and our gratitude to our patron Saint Augustine,” Arcay said.
He said the festival also reminds residents to protect Panglao’s natural and cultural treasures for future generations.
Panglao has experienced rapid growth as a tourism destination. Once a fourth-class municipality, it became a first-class municipality in 2022, largely due to the expansion of tourism.

blocks.caption: Saint Augustine of Hippo, patron saint of Panglao, Bohol

blocks.text: The Bohol-Panglao International Airport has helped make the town a major gateway to the province.
Panglao recorded around a million tourists in 2024 and more than 500,000 visitors during the first half of 2026, according to the local government.
The growth, however, has brought environmental challenges, including coral vandalism and the impact of mass tourism on the island’s natural resources.
Apart from its beaches, Panglao also has important cultural heritage sites.

The Panglao Parish Church of Saint Augustine, completed in 1924 under Bishop Juan Gorordo, is one of the town’s major landmarks. The church features Corinthian columns, ceiling paintings and machuca tile flooring.
The church was declared an Important Cultural Property in 2011 and sustained minimal damage during the 2013 Bohol earthquake.
Five cultural property markers were installed at the church complex by the National Museum of the Philippines in 2023.

Panglao’s tourism attractions also include Balicasag Island, known for its coral walls and marine life; Virgin Island, popular among snorkelers; and South Farm in Barangay Bolod, which features organic farming and tourism activities.
Through Hudyaka, Panglao continues to promote not only its beaches and tourism industry but also the faith, traditions, and stories that form part of its identity. /cb

blocks.text: August 29, 2026
Modi lands in Uzbekistan en route to Russia-Asia summit

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi posted pictures of himself and Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to social media on Saturday, thanking his political counterpart for the warm welcome and writing on X: "Landed in Tashkent to a warm welcome by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.
