articles.title: Russian drone strike on Kyiv warehouse storing weapons kills at least 37
articles.summary:
Ukrainian prosecutors open investigation into why munitions were stored so close to residential buildings

At least 37 people have been killed after a Russian drone struck a warehouse near…

blocks.text: At least 37 people have been killed after a Russian drone struck a warehouse near Kyiv’s western suburbs that was storing “explosive objects”.

The attack damaged at least 50 residential buildings, including a care home for elderly and disabled people, and sparked a huge fire and explosions in the Bucha district of the Kyiv region. The regional governor, Tymur Tkachenko, said a further 42 people, including four children, had been injured in the strike.

More than 370 people have been evacuated from the area and the evacuation process was continuing, the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said. In a statement, he said a warehouse in the town of Myla had been struck, “followed by a detonation”.

The warehouse was a depot owned by the Ukrainian military and stored shells, drones and other munitions, he said in a video address. “The first impact was on a place where ammunition was being stored that absolutely should not have been there – a depot of the defence forces. [There was] detonation of shells, mines, other munitions and drones on a significant scale,” Zelenskyy said.
Criminal proceedings had been opened on charges of official negligence, he added.
“There are regulations in place; ammunition cannot be stored near homes or other residential areas.”
He said one of the people killed was the head of the Dmytrivka community, Taras Didych, who died while rescuing others.

blocks.caption: Smoke and flames rise from the warehouse after the strike in the Bucha district of the Kyiv region. Photograph: Libkos/Getty

blocks.text: Ukrainian prosecutors said they had opened an investigation into the legality of the “storage of explosive objects and materials”.
The Ukrainian prime minister, Serhii Koretskyi, expressed regret that mistakes had not been learned from a previous deadly strike on a munitions depot in Vyshneve, near Kyiv, in July.

An investigation into that incident, in which 22 people were killed and fires tore through nearby homes, revealed serious failings on the part of a state-owned company, which did not comply with regulations on the proximity of residential buildings.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: A man walks past destroyed houses after the Russian strike in Bucha.  Photograph: Libkos/Getty

blocks.text: “Unfortunately, we can already see that the terrible tragedy in Vyshneve did not become a lesson,” Koretskyi said. “In the fifth year of a full-scale invasion, making the same mistakes is criminal negligence. And all those guilty, without exception, must be severely punished so that such situations do not happen again.”

In a statement, Russia’s ministry of defence said it had hit a warehouse in Myla storing components and launch boosters for long-range drones. It said it had also attacked the ports of Mykolaiv and Izmail, as well as a logistics centre and warehouse facilities storing parts for Ukraine’s Flamingo cruise missiles in the Kyiv region.
Elsewhere, Russian attacks across Ukraine’s southern Kherson region killed two people and wounded 27 more on Saturday, including a child, a local official said.

articles.title: F1: Lando Norris extends McLaren stay until 2030
articles.summary: LONDON–Reigning F1 world champion Lando Norris has committed his long-term future to McLaren after signing a contract extension that will keep him at the team until 2030. The new deal comes less than…

blocks.text: McLaren driver Lando Norris of Britain lifts the trophy after winning the Formula One Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort , Netherlands, Sunday, Aug. 23, 2026. (AP Photo/Darko Bandic)
LONDON–Reigning F1 world champion Lando Norris has committed his long-term future to McLaren after signing a contract extension that will keep him at the team until 2030.
The new deal comes less than a week after Norris secured back-to-back wins with victory at the Dutch Grand Prix, rekindling the British driver’s hopes of a successful defence of his world title.
It includes an option for a multi-year extension beyond 2030, McLaren said in its announcement on Saturday.
Last season, the 26-year-old Norris delivered McLaren’s first drivers’ title since Lewis Hamilton won it in 2008.
Norris joined McLaren’s junior program when he was just 17 and made his F1 debut two years later, in 2019.
“McLaren is my home, and I’m very pleased to be signing a new contract to keep me with the team until at least 2030,” Norris said in a team statement.
“When I started this journey nine years ago, I was clear about the goals I wanted to achieve: to get McLaren back to the front and to win championships.
“We’ve achieved that goal, but we want more, we want to keep on winning, and we know as a team that we’re capable of achieving it.”
Norris sits fourth in this year’s championship, trailing Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli by 83 points with 11 races left in the season.
His McLaren teammate Oscar Piastri extended his contract at the start of the 2025 season on a deal that is believed to run until at least 2028.

McLaren won constructors’ titles in 2024 and 2025, ending a championship drought that had stretched back to 1998, but the team was well off the pace at the start of this season after struggling to master the new rules.
Norris’s resurgence has shown there is still all to play for after wins in Hungary and the Netherlands with an improved car.
“Lando has been an integral part of McLaren’s journey and success over the last nine years, and we are delighted to continue our partnership with him,” said team principal Andrea Stella.

“He is an exceptional driver, someone who combines outstanding natural speed with maturity, consistency and a strong commitment to McLaren, but above all, he is a special human being who is valued by everyone in the team.”
Stella added: “With him and Oscar, we know we can count not only on one of the strongest partnerships but also on one of the most united and close-knit teams in Formula 1.”
Norris will also receive one of the MCL39 cars that he used to secure his first F1 title last year as a gift from the team.

articles.title: Prosecution panel not ruling out Lachica as witness in Sara Duterte impeachment trial
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel is not ruling out the possibility of presenting former Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group (VPSPG) commander Colonel Raymund Lachica as a witness in the…

blocks.text: Published August 29, 2026 9:30pm

The House prosecution panel is not ruling out the possibility of presenting former Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group (VPSPG) commander Colonel Raymund Lachica as a witness in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, according to former Surigao del Norte congressman Robert Ace Barbers.

Barbers, the designated adviser to the House prosecution panel, said they have yet to call Lachica to testify in connection with the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) alleged misuse of confidential funds because they do not need his testimony yet.

“Hindi sarado ang aming isipan para ipresenta si Colonel Lachica. Kung naniniwala kami na mayroong kakulangan o kinakailangan pang madagdagan ang evidentiary value or puwedeng sumuporta sa aming allegations, bakit hindi?” Barbers said on Saturday.
(Our minds are not closed to presenting Colonel Lachica. If we believe there is a gap, or we need to add evidentiary value or support our allegations, why not?)
Asked whether the prosecution was concerned that Lachica might take full responsibility for the alleged misuse of the funds, Barbers said they were prepared for such a possibility.

“Kung sakaling 'yan ang kanyang gagawin, it doesn't give us any evidentiary value doon sa allegations namin. Problema niya 'yun. Kung 'yun ang gagawin niya, siya 'yung mananagot sa batas,” Barbers said.
(If he does that, it doesn't give us any evidentiary value for our allegations. That is his problem. If that is what he does, he will be held accountable under the law.)
The defense also listed Lachica as a witness, so the prosecution is prepared to cross-examine him if he takes the stand, Barbers said.
During the August 17 hearing, former OVP Special Disbursing Officer Gina Acosta said that Duterte was the one who asked her to disburse P125 million in confidential funds to Lachica.
On August 25, Lachica expressed his readiness to appear before the Senate impeachment court “to tell the truth, subject to applicable laws and security restrictions.”
Barbers said the prosecution will present four more witnesses in the coming trial days: three officials from the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and defense counsel Michael Poa.
Poa is set to be designated as a hostile witness. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Tony Parker believes Wembanyama, Spurs are close to NBA glory
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — San Antonio Spurs legend Tony Parker sees a bright future in the Victor Wembanyama era, believing the franchise could win it all sooner rather than later. A four-time NBA…

blocks.text: San Antonio Spurs legend Tony Parker during his visit to Manila for the NBA House Philippines. –NBA PH PHOTO
MANILA, Philippines — San Antonio Spurs legend Tony Parker sees a bright future in the Victor Wembanyama era, believing the franchise could win it all sooner rather than later.
A four-time NBA champion and former Finals MVP, Parker is confident that Wembanyama and the Spurs can bring glory back to San Antonio after losing to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals last June.
“The potential is amazing. You know, I think it’s just a matter of time before they win the championship,” said Parker on Saturday during the launch of the NBA House at One Ayala in Makati.

WATCH: Tony Parker talks about his visit in the Philippines and the future of San Antonio Spurs with Victor Wembanyama. | @LanceAgcaoilINQ pic.twitter.com/fSB6fL1lCi — INQUIRER Sports (@inquirersports) August 29, 2026
The six-time NBA All-Star won championships in 2003, 2005, 2007 and 2014 with Tim Duncan and Manu Ginobili under coach Gregg Popovich.
Parker also had a storied international career with the France national basketball team, where Wembanyama also plays. France settled for silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics after losing to Team USA.
Like what he sees from the Spurs, the legendary point guard also believes Wembanyama can take France to greater heights.

blocks.caption: Victor Wembanyama Spurs vs Knicks Game 5 NBA Finals

blocks.text: San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama sits on the floor after a foul during the second half of Game 5 of the NBA Finals basketball series against the New York Knicks, Saturday, June 13, 2026, in San Antonio. (AP Photo/Ross D. Franklin)
“Same thing. I hope we get a lot of gold medals. I think we have a very, very good team. And now we just have to keep working hard,” he said.

The 44-year-old Parker has been enjoying his time in Manila, holding a basketball clinic for Filipino kids with WNBA legend Lauren Jackson on Saturday. He also coached celebrities against Jason Kidd in an exhibition game.

“I love it.. Every time I can share my experience and spend some time with the kids, I think it’s priceless. And I used to love it when I was that age. I always loved spending time with professional basketball players,” said Parker.
WATCH: Tony Parker is here to hold a basketball clinic for Filipino kids with Lauren Jackson. | @LanceAgcaoilINQ pic.twitter.com/sbcnKduMB2 — INQUIRER Sports (@inquirersports) August 29, 2026
“And I’m happy to be here. You can see the passion, the energy is amazing. And we know, you know, in the Philippines, they love the NBA.”
“Since I arrived the love here is amazing. And so, I love everything.”
Parker also stressed the importance of fundamentals to kids aspiring to become professional basketball players.

“I think that’s the basics, You have to start from there. So, that’s why those camps are very important. Every exercise we did today is the foundation, how you’re going to become a good player, a great player, if you want to go all the way to the NBA,” Parker said.

articles.title: Dizon inspects overflowing Sto. Cristo Dam as DPWH steps up flood mitigation efforts in Pampanga
articles.summary: LUBAO, Pampanga — Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon inspected the overflowing Sto. Cristo Dam in Lubao, Pampanga, amid continuous heavy rains that caused the Gumain…

blocks.text: Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon inspects overflowing Sto. Cristo Dam as DPWH steps up flood mitigation efforts in Pampanga. (Photo courtesy of DPWH III / via Liezle Inigo)

LUBAO, Pampanga — Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon inspected the overflowing Sto. Cristo Dam in Lubao, Pampanga, amid continuous heavy rains that caused the Gumain River to swell and contributed to flooding in parts of Barangay Sto. Cristo.
The overflow was linked to the accumulation of logs and other debris that obstructed the flow of water in the dam.
The situation reportedly damaged a portion of the dike, allowing floodwaters to spread into nearby areas.

During the inspection, Dizon assessed the condition of the dam and affected flood-control structures as the Department of Public Works and Highways intensified its response to the worsening flooding in the area.
Following President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s directive, the DPWH is conducting dredging operations to improve water flow and divert excess water from the Main River toward the Pasig-Potrero River.
Clearing operations are also underway to remove logs, garbage, and other obstructions.

articles.title: Cells for arrested offenders may run out without early prison release, says Labour
articles.summary:
Bridget Phillipson says government would not have to consider releasing prisoners early if Tories had created more capacity

Cells to hold newly arrested people could run out without the…

blocks.text: Cells to hold newly arrested people could run out without the early prison release scheme, a minister has said.

Bridget Phillipson defended the plan to address the prison capacity crisis in England and Wales by releasing thousands of prisoners early, which has been criticised by domestic abuse charities, bereaved families and probation officers among others.

“We have faced some really difficult and unpalatable choices because of the huge crisis that was left behind in the prisons estate,” the women and equalities minister told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme on Saturday.
She insisted the “most serious offenders” would not be released early under the scheme, details of which would be set out during the week.

“But the reality of what we are confronting is that, if allowed to go unchecked, we could end up in a position where someone who was arrested for very serious offences, for example, offences related to violence against a woman, and we wouldn’t have anywhere to send that individual. That was the full scale of the real crisis we face.”

Andy Burnham has been facing pressure to balance the competing aims of creating space in prisons and avoiding causing further upset to victims of serious crime. Under the scheme, a sentence would not be ended early but the portion of it served in custody would be shortened. The remainder would be served in the community, a principle that already exists in most sentences.

On Friday, families of those affected by homicide called for those convicted of any form of manslaughter to be excluded from the scheme. In a letter to the justice secretary, Alex Norris, they said they felt victims were “being asked to bear the consequences of the prison capacity crisis”.

Signatories included Emma Webber, whose son Barnaby was stabbed to death in Nottingham in 2023 and whose killer, Valdo Calocane, was convicted of manslaughter on the basis of diminished responsibility. Another was Diana Parkes, whose daughter Joanna Simpson was killed by her estranged husband, Robert Brown, in 2010. Brown was also convicted of manslaughter on the basis of diminished responsibility.

Phillipson said she had the “utmost respect and sympathy for the victims and their families” and blamed the previous Conservative government for allowing the prison capacity problem to fester. “We didn’t create enough prison capacity in the years that they were in government so that we don’t have to be even considering these kinds of options, which – in an ideal world – we would not be having to consider.”
after newsletter promotion

In January, the government announced a set of measures, which came into force in March, that were designed to stave off a looming crisis this summer. Sources indicated, however, that these measures were never thought to be enough to avert further crises. They pointed to the Sentencing Act, which introduces wholesale changes to sentencing, as the government’s plan to fix the issue once and for all.

articles.title: Lachica testimony not needed to prove VP misused confidential funds – Barbers
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – The House impeachment team does not need Col. Raymund Dante Lachica’s testimony to establish its allegation that Vice President Sara Z. Duterte misused confidential…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The House impeachment team does not need Col. Raymund Dante Lachica’s testimony to establish its allegation that Vice President Sara Z. Duterte misused confidential funds, its adviser and spokesperson Ace Barbers said Saturday.
Barbers said evidence already presented before the impeachment court was sufficient to establish Duterte’s role as the head of the agency and approving authority over the confidential funds.

“Hindi namin kailangan iyong kanyang testimonya para makapagbigay-lakas o diin dito sa aming allegation,” Barbers said, referring to Lachica, during the Saturday News Forum at Dapo Restaurant in Quezon City.

Lachica, former security chief of the Office of the Vice President (OVP), figured prominently in the testimony of two hostile witnesses presented by the prosecution—former OVP special disbursing officer (SDO) Gina Acosta and Assistant Secretary and Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio.

Acosta testified that she turned over four P125-million tranches of OVP confidential funds to Lachica upon Duterte’s instruction even though he was not the SDO or fidelity-bonded accountable officer for the money.

She also testified that she did not personally witness how the money was distributed and relied on reports and assurances from Lachica in preparing the liquidation documents for which she remained the accountable officer.
Ortonio, meanwhile, testified that Duterte approved the confidential fund disbursement vouchers and liquidation reports.
He also confirmed that only the vice president, as head of agency, and Lachica, as her chief security officer, had personal knowledge of how the confidential funds were actually implemented.

Barbers said the prosecution believes these testimonies, together with those of Land Bank of the Philippines officials and Commission on Audit auditors, already support its allegations under Article I pertaining to Duterte’s misused of confidential funds.

He dismissed the possibility that prosecutors were holding back from calling Lachica out of concern that the security officer could take responsibility for the transactions and shield Duterte from accountability.
“Anuman ang sasabihin niya na maaaring maka-turn around o maka-turn ng aming presentation ng ebidensya, sa aming paniwala, it will not matter. It will not matter,” Barbers said.

“Kasi matibay na at sufficient na sa ngayon, sa puntong ito, na itong mga witnesses na pinresenta namin ay nakapagbigay-lakas at magbibigay ng diin doon sa aming allegations of misuse, misappropriation, at of course, itong sinasabi nating irregular liquidation,” he added.
Barbers also rejected suggestions that the prosecution is afraid to put Lachica on the witness stand.
“Ba’t naman matatakot sa kanya?” he said.
He recalled that the House Committee on Good Government and Public Accountability repeatedly summoned Lachica during its 2024 inquiry into Duterte’s confidential funds, but he did not appear.
“Eh unang-una, tinatawag namin siya noon sa Committee on Good Government. Hindi naman siya humarap. Ilang beses siya pinatawag, hindi rin siya humarap,” Barbers said.
Barbers noted that the prosecution has already presented hostile witnesses who worked closely with Duterte.

“So hindi kami dapat matakot because tatlo na nga iyong hostile witness na pinresenta natin, mas malalapit ito sa ating Pangalawang Pangulo, di ba? At kailangan pa ba kami magdagdag ng pang-apat? Sa aking paniwala, hindi,” he said.

The prosecution is expected to next present Duterte defense lawyer and former Department of Education undersecretary and chief of staff Michael Wesley Poa. It plans to ask the impeachment court to declare him its third hostile witness.
As for Lachica, Barbers said the prosecution sees no need to call him at this point but is keeping the option open should his testimony later become necessary.

articles.summary: BAYAMBANG, Pangasinan — Bayambang Mayor Nina Jose Quiambao has ordered the implementation of forced evacuation in 36 barangays located along the Agno River amid continued rainfall and the anticipated…

blocks.text: BAYAMBANG, Pangasinan — Bayambang Mayor Nina Jose Quiambao has ordered the implementation of forced evacuation in 36 barangays located along the Agno River amid continued rainfall and the anticipated increase in water flow that could threaten lives and property.
In a public advisory issued August 29, Quiambao directed residents living along riverbanks and in low-lying, flood-prone areas to immediately evacuate to safer locations.
The order was issued as a precautionary measure against the possible rise of water levels in the Agno River.
This may result in flooding and pose serious risks to communities situated near the river.
Residents were urged to coordinate with their respective barangay officials and strictly follow the directives of authorities.
They were also advised not to wait for floodwaters to reach dangerous levels before evacuating.

The 36 barangays covered by the directive are Amancosiling Norte, Amancosiling Sur, Ambayat 1st, Ambayat 2nd, Ataynan, Bacnono, Bongato East, Bongato West, Buenlag 1st, Buenlag 2nd, Carungay, Darawe, Hermoza, Iton, Malioer, Managos, Manambong Norte, Manambong Parte, Manambong Sur, Mangayao, Nalsian Norte, Nalsian Sur, Pangdel, Pantol, Paragos, Poblacion Sur, Pugo, Reynado, San Gabriel 1st, San Vicente, San Gabriel 2nd, Tamaro, Tambac, Tampog, Warding, and Wawa.
Quiambao appealed to residents to cooperate with local authorities and prioritize their safety as monitoring of the Agno River and surrounding areas continues.

articles.title: LTFRB summons 21 bus, UV Express operators for various violations
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines—The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) on Saturday said it has summoned 21 operators of buses and UV express units for violating the rules at the Edsa…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) on Saturday said it has summoned 21 operators of buses and UV express units for violating the rules at the Edsa Busway as well as operating dilapidated units.
In a statement, the agency said show cause orders were issued to bus operators following the deployment of “mystery riders.”

The “mystery riders” were tasked with monitoring bus drivers who deliberately slow down their buses, with the LTFRB noting that traffic enforcers have been directed to implement a 30-second rule in bus stops.
It added that two drivers and a bus conductor were also apprehended along Edsa Busway for smoking inside the vehicle.

Show cause orders were also issued to several operators of UV Express services over their use of “dilapidated and smelly” vehicles following complaints from passengers, with the majority of the vehicles were apprehended along routes in Bulacan going to Metro Manila
The LTFRB said their violations included having a non-functioning air conditioner, faded paints, a “dilapidated” chair and an “unpleasant” smell inside the vehicle.
All the operators who received the summons were asked to explain why their franchise should not be revoked or suspended amid their violations.

Amid the issuance of show cause orders, acting LTFRB chairperson Greg Pua Jr. urged operators of public utility vehicles (PUVs) to follow the rules and regulations that were established to ensure a safe and comfortable transportation.
“There are conditions that PUV operators are mandated to comply with—all of them are anchored on road safety and professionalism of the country’s public land transportation system,” he said.
“Accountability comes for those who chose to defy or ignore these conditions, and this is what the LTFRB did in the case of these 21 bus and UV Express operators,” added Pua. /gsg

Chinese state media earlier confirmed seven dead in Tibet following Wednesday’s disaster, taking the total killed to 682.
The number of missing in Nepal remained constant at 2,426, after a sharp hike in numbers on Saturday morning.

That missing list includes 517 foreigners, as well as 933 workers on hydropower projects on the river where the torrent smashed down, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.
The number of missing also includes 45 Nepali Army soldiers, 40 police officers, and 19 immigration and customs officers.
In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims. However, they are not included in the toll.

items: The US Embassy in Manila warned that submitting fake documents or misrepresenting facts in visa applications can result in denial, criminal prosecution, and a lifetime ban from entering the United States.
The embassy said it recently notified Philippine law enforcement about a visa fraud case that resulted in the arrest of an applicant who used fake documents.
US consular officers who discover fraudulent Philippine documents notify Philippine authorities, the embassy said.

blocks.text: US Embassy in Manila (MB File Photo)

The US Embassy in Manila has warned visa applicants against submitting fake documents or misrepresenting facts, saying such acts can lead to criminal prosecution, arrest, and a lifetime ban from entering the United States.
In an X post on Saturday, Aug. 29, the embassy said it recently notified Philippine law enforcement about a visa fraud case that resulted in the arrest of an applicant who used fake documents.
The embassy said its consular officers notify Philippine government authorities whenever they discover fraudulent Philippine documents during the visa application process.
"Using fake documents or misrepresenting facts can result in a lifetime ban from entering the United States as well as criminal prosecution and arrest," the embassy said in an accompanying video.
The warning applies to applicants who attempt to support their visa applications with falsified documents or provide false information to US consular officers.
The embassy emphasized that visa fraud is treated as a serious offense and that applicants should not assume fraudulent submissions will go undetected.
"Walang sikreto. No secrets, no exceptions, no tolerance for fraud," the embassy said.
The embassy urged anyone with information about visa fraud to report it to [email protected].

articles.title: Niger's defense ministry says soldiers attempted mutiny
articles.summary: Gunfire and explosions were heard across Niamey overnight. The attack posed the latest threat to Niger's military junta, led by Abdourahamane Tchiani, who seized power in a 2023 coup.
articles.byline: Emmy Sasipornkarn, Dharvi Vaid Dhulia, Zac Crellin

image.caption: The main airport in Niamey was reportedly targeted by the attacks [FILE: August 8, 2026]Image: Sam Mednick/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Niger's Ministry of National Defense ‌on ⁠Saturday said ⁠that ​a group of soldiers shot at "sensitive" locations in the capital Niamey in an apparent mutiny.
Gunfire and explosions had been heard across Niger's capital, Niamey, overnight into the early hours of Saturday morning.
Attackers had targeted Diori Hamani International Airport, which also houses a military air base, and attempted to breach the security perimeter around ​the presidency.
"Another cowardly attack on Base 101 and once again our defense and security forces ensured ... Situation under control," said lawmaker Bana Wagana Ibrahim, who serves on the Consultative Council.
Niger military 'gradually regaining control'
The military said it was "gradually regaining control" after mutineers took soldiers hostage at a base near the airport in Niamey, AFP news agency reported.
Authorities urged the public to "remain calm and freely go about their business" in a statement read out on public television and signed by Defense Minister General Salifou Mody.
The attack posed the latest threat to Niger's military junta, led by Abdourahamane Tchiani, who seized power in a 2023 coup.
Niger, like its Sahelian neighbors Mali and Burkina Faso, has for years been ruled by a military junta that has struggled to stem a jihadi insurgency.
National TV signal reportedly cut after gunfire
The shooting began around 1 a.m. local time (0000 GMT) and continued until daybreak.
Locals said that the country's national television had gone off air.
Tele Sahel's satellite and online programming was replaced with a black screen at 9 a.m. local time (0800 GMT), AFP reported. It was restored around one hour later.

Niamey has been targeted by jihadists twice this year: once by the so-called "Islamic State in the Sahel" group (EIS) and again in June by their rivals from the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM).

articles.title: DOLE orders contractor of collapsed Pampanga building to pay P11.49M in wages, fines
articles.summary: The Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) on Saturday said the contractor behind the collapsed building in Angeles City, Pampanga is liable for P11.49 million in unpaid wages and administrative…

blocks.text: Published August 29, 2026 8:14pm

The Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) on Saturday said the contractor behind the collapsed building in Angeles City, Pampanga is liable for P11.49 million in unpaid wages and administrative fines.

In a statement, the DOLE said Golden Years Construction and Steelworks Corporation and building owner Ernest Jackson Lim failed to pay workers’ benefits and committed occupational safety and health (OSH) violations even before the building collapsed.

“The amount includes P1.17 million in unpaid wages during the Work Stoppage Order (WSO), underpaid wages, unpaid rest day premiums and holiday pay, as well as P10.32 million in administrative fines for OSH violations,” the DOLE said.
The decision stemmed from a resolution signed by DOLE Secretary Francis Tolentino on August 17.
The DOLE said the workers’ claims were meritorious, including their entitlement to rest day premiums during the implementation of the work stoppage order from October 16 to 24, 2025.

“A review of the records established several serious OSH violations, including failure to provide personal protective equipment, secure required permits for mechanical lifting equipment, deploy required safety officers and first aiders, and provide temporary accommodation for workers,” the agency said.
The DOLE also found that fake and invalid certificates had been submitted for the project’s first aider and safety officer.
The respondents were ordered to pay the monetary award and administrative fines within 10 days of receiving the resolution.
The nine-story building under construction collapsed before dawn on May 24, killing 30 people. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Laurie Anderson’s next manuscript to be locked away for 88 years in Future Library
articles.summary:
Grammy award-winning American artist selected as 13th person to submit written work to Oslo-based project

The next manuscript by the American artist Laurie Anderson will remain unseen for 88…
articles.byline: Nadia Khomami Arts and culture correspondent

blocks.text: The next manuscript by the American artist Laurie Anderson will remain unseen for 88 years, as she becomes the 13th figure to contribute to the Future Library project.
Anderson joins Margaret Atwood, Han Kang, Ocean Vuong and other prominent authors who have written secret manuscripts, which have been locked away until 2114.

The texts are stored in a specially designed silent room in the Deichman Bjørvika building at the public library in Oslo. At the end of the project, the full anthology of texts will be printed using paper made from trees from the Future Library forest in Nordmarka, in northern Oslo, where 1,000 spruce trees were planted by Katie Paterson, the artist behind the project, in 2014.
Anderson is a writer, director, composer, visual artist, musician and vocalist whose work spans art, theatre, experimental music and technology.

She has created numerous multimedia stage performances and published 10 books, as well as being nominated for six Grammy Awards, winning once and receiving a lifetime achievement award in 2024. Her visual art has been exhibited globally at institutions including the Hirshhorn Museum in Washington DC and Moderna Museet in Stockholm.
Anderson’s manuscript for the project may be a text, a score, a story, a set of instructions or “something for which we do not yet have a name”, Paterson said.

blocks.caption: Laurie Anderson performs in Amsterdam in 1982. Photograph: Rob Verhorst/Redferns

blocks.text: Anderson said: “I absolutely loved the idea of the Future Library as soon as I learned about it. I’ve always been in love with books, libraries and forests. When I was a kid we lived next to a large park filled with maple, elm and oak trees. At the far corner of the park was an enormous red oak tree and up the street and just around the bend, there was the library, a rustic fieldstone building filled with comfortable pillows and many thousands of books.

“‘You better check with grandfather tree today if you have the time,’ my mother would say some mornings. In a house where candy of all kinds was forbidden, we knew what that meant: there would be chocolate bars and chocolate mints up in the fork of the red oak, just low enough for us to hoist ourselves up and grab them. It also meant that we’d have extra incentive that day to get to the library.”

Anderson called her mother a “brilliant and unhappy woman”. She said she should have been a chief executive of a large corporation but instead had eight children. “She loved books and somehow made it a project to get up early in the morning, walk through the park and hide chocolate bars in a tree. She taught us to love books, magic and old trees.

“I’m hoping to be able to write something useful about love for the people who will read this in 2114. My favourite books are the ones in which I can hear someone’s voice, which is why I’ll try my best to make myself clear to the people who come across these books in the next century.”

The Future Library Trust said it had selected Anderson for her “singular ability to speak across time, creating work that is profoundly human, radically imaginative and alive to futures we cannot yet foresee”.

Paterson added: “Laurie Anderson has spent a lifetime sending signals into the unknown. For decades, she has explored how we tell stories, how we remember, and how we imagine what is yet to come. Moving freely between language, music, visual art, technology and performance, her work travels between the intimate and the planetary, love and loss, politics and poetry, with humour, tenderness and wonder.”

Other writers to have contributed to the project include David Mitchell, Sjón, Elif Shafak, Karl Ove Knausgård, Tsitsi Dangarembga, Judith Schalansky, Valeria Luiselli, Tommy Orange and, most recently, Amitav Ghosh.
In June 2022, the City of Oslo signed an agreement that ensures the forest will remain in the hands of the Future Library Trust for the duration of the project.

articles.title: Habagat rains persist, trigger flooding, evacuations in parts of Luzon
articles.summary: Continuous heavy rains brought by the Southwest Monsoon, or Habagat, caused flooding in several areas in Luzon on Saturday, August 29, 2026.

blocks.text: Published August 29, 2026 7:42pm
Continuous heavy rains brought by the Southwest Monsoon, or Habagat, caused flooding in several areas in Luzon on Saturday, August 29, 2026.
Pangasinan
In Dagupan City, several roads were submerged in floodwaters. Aside from the continuous rains, authorities also cited the high tide, which peaked at more than three feet, as a contributing factor.
Several residents in Agno evacuated after local authorities advised families living in flood-prone areas to leave their homes.

As of 10:26 a.m., the Agno Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO) reported that the road leading to Cayungnan Road was completely submerged and impassable to all types of vehicles.
Several residents of a barangay in Aguilar also evacuated as authorities reminded communities in flood-prone areas to undertake preemptive evacuations as early as possible.

Barangay Councilor Bryson Ian Soriano shared footage online showing deep, river-like flooding along a road in Barangay Bongalon, Labrador, amid the continuous downpour. Vehicles, particularly light vehicles, were struggling to pass, while floodwaters had entered several homes in the area.

In a social media update, GMA Regional TV reporter Sendee Salvacio reported that some residents of Barangay Talibaew in Calasiao were using makeshift rafts, or balsa, as floodwaters continued to rise.
According to Salvacio, the water level at the Marusay River had surpassed the critical mark. The Calasiao MDRRMO continued to monitor flooded and low-lying areas.
Aside from flooding, a landslide was also reported along a portion of the Macaboboni-Abagatanen Road in Agno. The road was temporarily impassable, and motorists were advised to avoid the area.
Pampanga
Capitol Boulevard in Lelut Baculut, San Fernando City, Pampanga was no longer passable to light vehicles as of 1:40 p.m. due to rising floodwaters. Motorists were advised to exercise extra caution.
Bataan
In Balanga, some residents experienced ankle-deep flooding on Saturday, according to an update from GMA News reporter Bea Pinlac.
Meanwhile, YouScooper Jimmy Mangalindan shared footage showing calf-deep flooding in Balanga City at around 11:30 a.m.
Mangalindan said floodwaters in other parts of the barangay had reached chest level due to an overflowing river.
Bulacan
Flooding also affected a stretch of MacArthur Highway in Marilao, Bulacan, according to GMA News reporter Jamie Santos.
Several commuters were seen hitching rides on trucks to cross the flooded road, while others waded through the water.
Santos also reported deep flooding along MacArthur Highway in Meycauayan, where floodwaters ranged from thigh- to waist-deep.
Tarlac
In Tarlac City, a portion of the Aquino Bridge collapsed at around 11:56 p.m. on Friday, prompting authorities to temporarily close the bridge to motorists.
Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon inspected the bridge, where a section measuring about 60 meters long had collapsed.
The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) said strong river currents caused by the Habagat rains hit the bridge’s foundation, resulting in the collapse. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Cops, soldiers help rebuild damaged bamboo bridge in Oriental Mindoro
articles.summary: Policemen and soldiers were deployed to a barangay in Bongabong town of Oriental Mindoro and helped rebuild a temporary bridge and reconnect a community that were earlier isolated when the bamboo…

blocks.text: Policemen and soldiers were deployed to a barangay in Bongabong town of Oriental Mindoro and helped rebuild a temporary bridge and reconnect a community that were earlier isolated when the bamboo bridge was away by strong river current.

The deployment of police and military personnel came a few days after members of the 2nd Provincial Mobile Force Company (PMFC), Oriental Mindoro Police Provincial Office rescued 12 teachers who were stranded when the bridge in Sitio Naswak in Barangay Lisap collapsed on Aug. 20.

Brig. Gen. Christopher dela Cruz, director of Police Regional Office 4-B covering the Mimaropa region, said the collapse of the bamboo bridge cut off the usual passage to and from Sitio Naswak and made it difficult for residents to travel to the main community

“Police and Army helped construct the temporary bridge to provide a passable route for residents while longer-term arrangements are being addressed by the concerned local authorities,” said dela Cruz.
The unformed personnel were assisted by barangay officials and local residents.

Dela Cruz commended the police personnel, soldiers, local officials, and residents who took part in the undertaking, “Our responsibility does not end when the rescue is over. When our communities need help getting back on their feet, we should be there with them.”

“What happened in Naswak shows what can be done when the police, military, local government, and community work together. Everyone had a part in helping restore a basic need of the people—a safe way to get home,” he added.
Dela Cruz said the temporary bridge now provides the residents of Sitio Naswak with a restored passage as the community continues to recover from the effects of the flooding.

articles.title: Raided steel firm possibly being used as entryway for undocumented Chinese nationals --AFP
articles.summary: The steel factories recently raided by authorities were possibly being used as a possible point of entry for Chinese nationals who want to illegally enter and stay in the Philippines, according to…

blocks.text: Published August 29, 2026 7:06pm

The steel factories recently raided by authorities were possibly being used as a possible point of entry for Chinese nationals who want to illegally enter and stay in the Philippines, according to Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea Rear Admiral Roy Trinidad.
“It is a possible point of entry ng mga undocumented Chinese nationals na pwede kumalat sa area at magkaroon pa ng mas malaking threats sa ating security,” Trinidad said on the Saturday News Forum.
(It is a possible point of entry for undocumented Chinese nationals that could spread in the area and become a major threat to our security.)
Officials recently raided the Sanjia Steel Corp. in Misamis Oriental due to the facility being allegedly substandard.
There, they found 69 Chinese workers, many of whom are undocumented.
The Sanjia firm is one of five steel plants raided by the Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission and the National Bureau of Investigation, with the AFP providing additional support.

Trinidad said that Misamis Oriental steel factory was located near a Philippine Veterans Investment Development Corporation Industrial Authority, an Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement site, the 4th Infantry Division of the Philippine Army, and the Laguindingan International Airport.
He likened it to how Philippine Offshore Gaming Operators were placed near critical government infrastructure.
According to Trinidad, around 500 steel plants were closed in China due to their materials being substandard and some of them went to the Philippines.
Authorities are still determining how these steel factories were established in the Philippines in such a short amount of time, Trinidad said.
GMA News Online has reached out to the Chinese Embassy in the Philippines for a comment and will update the story once it responds. Misamis Oriental —VAL, GMA News

articles.summary: Dizon sits down with Rappler to talk about his beginnings in music, what it's like for him to move from genre to genre as the drummer of TEETH, Sandwich, and Pedicab, and how he discovered his love…

blocks.text: Dizon sits down with Rappler to talk about his beginnings in music, what it's like for him to move from genre to genre as the drummer of TEETH, Sandwich, and Pedicab, and how he discovered his love for documenting the restaurants he comes across
MANILA, Philippines – It’s not every day that an artist finds himself being a part of three of the Philippines’ most influential bands at the same time, until you meet Mike Dizon.

Dizon co-founded the alternative rock and grunge outfit TEETH in 1993. Years later, he also began playing the drums for rock band Sandwich and electronic rock band Pedicab. He is also a prolific songwriter, and is the mind behind hit songs like “Laklak” and “Prinsesa” by TEETH.
Outside of music, though, Dizon runs a successful YouTube channel, where he visits local eateries to try out the best dishes on the menu.

Ahead of TEETH’s reunion concert tour in celebration of their 33 years as a band, Dizon sits down with Rappler to talk about his beginnings in music, what it’s like for him to move from genre to genre, and how he discovered his love for documenting the restaurants he comes across.
Catch the full interview at 7 pm on Saturday, August 29, by bookmarking this page or heading to Rappler’s YouTube! – Rappler.com

articles.title: An island mysteriously appeared — then disappeared — on B.C.'s largest reservoir
articles.summary: B.C. Hydro says it's monitoring for the reappearance of a mysterious island first spotted by boaters 100 kilometres from the W.A.C. Bennett Dam in northeastern B.C.

image.caption: A photo of this floating island of trees in the Williston Lake reservoir in northern B.C. was taken by a local boater and shared with resident Rocky Avery, who posted it to social media in early August. (Submitted by Rocky Avery)

blocks.text: British Columbia
B.C. Hydro says it's monitoring for the reappearance of a mysterious island first spotted by boaters 100 kilometres from the W.A.C. Bennett Dam in northeastern B.C.
B.C. Hydro monitoring for island's reappearance after being spotted 100 kilometres from W.A.C. Bennett Dam
No one knows where it came from or where it went, but a massive new island might be floating out somewhere in the Williston Reservoir in northern B.C.
The forested land mass caught the attention of B.C. Hydro and local residents earlier this month after it was spotted bobbing in the massive man-made lake north of Mackenzie.
Rocky Avery says video and pictures of the island were taken by a boater and later shared with him. He posted them on social media, and they quickly went viral.
"It was a pretty amazing sight to see, never seen anything like that in my 40 years in this country," said Avery.

"There was a big fishing derby coming up, so I wanted to make sure everybody was aware of what was going on. And I wanted B.C. Hydro to know too that it was out there, just in case it was floating down their way."
The discovery left a B.C. Hydro spokesperson incredulous when CBC News first inquired about the island's origins.

Bob Gammer says he was first skeptical about the origins of the video because of the rise of generative AI technology. Not everything posted online can be trusted as being credible at first glance, he said.
"It's certainly something we've not heard of before," said Gammer. "And with not very many people reporting it, it was difficult to locate."
LISTEN | Floating island on Williston Reservoir:
Radio West3:57A floating island in northern B.C.'s Williston Reservoir
But satellite imagery dated July 21 confirmed the island was in fact real, and floating in the main body of the reservoir west of Finlay Bay, about 100 kilometres west of the W.A.C. Bennett Dam.
Gammer says the island was estimated around 70 metres wide and 140 metres long, or about 9,800 square metres in area.
According to those estimates, that's roughly the size of two NFL football fields.
By Aug. 5, the island was no longer showing up in satellite data.
"We've been taking more updated snapshots and we can't see the object anymore. So it's disappeared now," Gammer said.
"It doesn't mean it's gone to the bottom of the reservoir. It may have returned to a more sheltered area along the shoreline."
Gammer says no operational impacts are expected, though B.C. Hydro is monitoring for the island's possible reappearance.
First full reservoir in 14 years
The Williston reservoir, impounded behind the W.A.C. Bennett Dam in 1968, is the seventh-largest reservoir in the world and visible from space.
High winter snowpacks and steady summer rains have filled it to the brim, forcing B.C. Hydro to open the dam's spillways in June and July to release water.
Gammer says it's likely the island formed over many years somewhere along the shore where driftwood accumulated, allowing plants and trees to take root in the decomposing debris.

items: B.C. Hydro expects return to being net electricity exporter with surplus production in forecast

blocks.text: As reservoir levels rose, it broke free, and winds carried it out into open water.
"We haven't had a full reservoir in 14 years," Gammer said. "We can't pinpoint the origin of this floating island [but that's] one explanation that seems reasonable."
Avery says this year's high water has washed out shoreline sand dunes popular for quad-biking, and pulled more trees and debris out into the lake than usual.
"There's areas we would never even drive a boat on before, and now we're going up over top of it," said Avery.
Phenomenon seen across the world
While a rare sight in Williston Lake, floating islands are a rather common phenomenon seen in dam building.
In Wisconsin, massive chunks of peat bog broke off from the bottom of Lake Chippewa after it was flooded for the Winter Dam.
One of them, called the "Forty Acre Bog," has to be pushed by boat every year to prevent it from drifting into a local bridge.

In Africa, researchers are investigating how floating islands in Lake Victoria are impacting transportation, fisheries and water quality. The world's second-largest freshwater lake spans across three countries.
Lake needs public help to monitor
Gammer says the power utility relies on public reports in monitoring its reservoirs.
Because the Williston reservoir is so huge, he says it's not feasible to surveil it by water, and that B.C. Hydro will keep an eye out for sightings of the island via satellite.

items: More stories from Northern B.C.

blocks.text: Avery says local tugboat crews do a good job pulling what logs they can out of the lake, but says people need to be careful boating on the waters.
"When it's calm, it's fine. You can usually see them, but you get a little bit of choppy waves and it's really hard to see them until you're right on top," he said.
"Some are full-size trees and it'll do a lot of damage to your boat. So you got to be super careful."

articles.title: Gee Canlas speaks out on Archie Alemania marriage
articles.summary: Gee Canlas has spoken at length about her marriage to Archie Alemania, offering her side of their troubled relationship days after the actor publicly discussed their separation and described his own…

blocks.text: Gee Canlas has spoken at length about her marriage to Archie Alemania, offering her side of their troubled relationship days after the actor publicly discussed their separation and described his own perspective as a husband.
In a recent interview with Ogie Diaz, Gee disputed the picture of their marriage presented by Archie and recounted several incidents she said she endured while they were together.

Archie had earlier spoken about their relationship in an interview with Diaz, saying their marriage suffered because they had conflicting ideas about their roles as husband and wife. He also acknowledged that he had hit Gee with a tumbler during one confrontation.
Gee's account went further, as she described what she said were repeated instances of physical abuse.
She clarified he hit her with a stainless-steel tumbler during an argument. Gee said the impact was strong enough for her to hear what she described as the sound of her skull.
She also recalled another confrontation that she said left her with two fractured ribs.
According to Gee, Archie was preparing to leave during an argument when she tried to stop him. She said he pushed her before punching her in the side, leaving her unable to catch her breath.
Gee said she eventually curled up in pain and later sought medical treatment, where she learned that two of her ribs were fractured.
She said she had kept the incident from her father at the time because she wanted to protect Archie and preserve their family.
“This is the first time na malalaman ito ng dad ko,” Gee said in the interview.
She added that she could take responsibility for her own behavior during arguments but could not accept responsibility for being physically hurt.
“I can only take responsibility for my actions. I can't take responsibility for someone hurting me,” she said.
Gee also recalled what happened after she went to the hospital. She said she spent New Year recovering and was distressed when she later saw photos of Archie and his family celebrating together.
The actress said these experiences were among the reasons she eventually decided to leave the marriage.
Gee and Archie married in October 2018.
Last March, Gee confirmed on "Fast Talk with Boy Abunda"that they had separated and that she was the one who ultimately left the marriage.
Gee stressed that she was prepared to substantiate the claims she made in the interview.
“Everything I say in this interview is backed with evidence,” she said.

articles.title: Judicial and Bar Council opens application for next Supreme Court chief justice
articles.summary: Marcos will get to pick the next chief justice after Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo's retirement in November

blocks.text: HIGH COURT. In this file photo, the Supreme Court is holding oral arguments on the national budget and unprogrammed funds on April 7, 2026.
Supreme Court
Marcos will get to pick the next chief justice after Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo's retirement in November

MANILA, Philippines – The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) on Saturday, August 29, announced the opening of application for the next Supreme Court (SC) chief justice due to the upcoming retirement of Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo.

The new chief magistrate, who will be chosen by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., will replace Gesmundo who will retire on November 6. Under the rule, justices are mandated to retire from the judiciary when they reach the age of 70.

The Judicial and Bar Council (@JBC_Ph) has announced the opening, for application, the position of #SupremeCourtPH Chief Justice (vice Hon. Alexander G. Gesmundo, who will compulsorily retire on November 6, 2026).Read the full text of the Announcement and the guidelines on… pic.twitter.com/OlxIxSyI2X— Philippine Supreme Court Public Information Office (@SCPh_PIO) August 29, 2026

The next chief magistrate will be the country’s 28th Chief Justice and will sit at the SC’s top post. The High Court oversees all courts in the country, including high level courts like the Sandiganbayan, Court of Appeals, and the Court of Tax Appeals.

Gesmundo has been the chief justice since April 2021 upon the appointment of former president Rodrigo Duterte. Sources and court people alike often refer to Gesmundo as the High Court’s “stabilizing force” for introducing a concept of collegiality among the justices and reforms inside the SC.
Meanwhile, Gesmundo’s replacement will be chosen by Marcos after a screening process to be led by JBC. Public interviews will be held as well as part of this process.
Apart from Gesmundo, Associate Justice Amy Lazaro Javier is also retiring in November.

This gives Marcos two new appointments to the High Court after his first pick in 2025, Associate Justice Raul Villanueva. (READ: IN NUMBERS: Things to know about the Philippine Supreme Court and its justices)
Once Gesmundo and Lazaro Javier retire, the Duterte appointees inside the SC will drop to 10; Marcos might have three, while former president Benigno Aquino III has two. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Was it a mistake for 99 Colombian guerrillas to lay down their arms?
articles.summary:
Fighters in legal limbo after accepting ‘total peace’ plan of Petro government just days before hardliner Abelardo De la Espriella took over

In mid-June, 99 guerrilla fighters were flown by…
articles.byline: Daniela Díaz in Valle del Guamuez and Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro

blocks.text: In mid-June, 99 guerrilla fighters were flown by helicopter to a small settlement in a rural area of southern Colombia where they lined up and, one by one, handed their weapons to government officials: rifles, pistols, machine guns and grenade launchers.

They also stripped off their heavy tactical vests, field packs and camouflage uniforms, which were each piled into a bonfire to mark the beginning of a new life away from an armed conflict that has claimed nearly half a million lives in the last six decades.

That was precisely what the former president Gustavo Petro’s “total peace” plan had sought to achieve: negotiating with and disarming all of Colombia’s criminal groups, which are estimated to have nearly 30,000 members.

But the group of just 99 people was the only one to disarm, and did so just three days before the presidential runoff, which was won by the far-right millionaire lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella, who had campaigned on a promise to end “total peace” and return to a full-on strategy of jailing or killing criminals.

Now, several weeks after the new president took office – and amid efforts to deal with the aftermath of the 7.4-magnitude earthquake, as his government has already begun the promised airstrikes against criminal groups – the 99 do not know what will happen to them.

“We’re in limbo,” said Natalia Bríñez, 29, one of 13 women among the group staying in the temporary location zone, or ZUT by its Spanish initials, a government-controlled zone where, under surveillance and unable to leave, they were supposed to make the transition to civilian life over the following months.

blocks.caption: Natalia Briñez, a former guerrilla fighter, is one of 13 women in the ZUT. Photograph: Daniela Díaz/The Guardian

blocks.text: The former guerrillas are housed in beige brick buildings decorated with drawings they painted themselves, including doves of peace, with a communal dining hall where three meals a day are served. No weapons are allowed inside and soldiers guard the ZUT from a perimeter less than a mile away.

One former combatant built a makeshift gym with weights made from metal pipes and tins filled with cement and sand, and there is an improvised football pitch, but most of them spend their days on their phones.

De la Espriella has repeatedly said his government will no longer negotiate peace agreements and has yet to announce what he intends to do regarding the people at the ZUT. The president has not responded to requests for comment.

In theory, any arrest warrants against the group are suspended, and they remain under state protection until 25 December, when Petro’s decree establishing the ZUT expires. But De la Espriella could revoke the decree at any time.

Armando Novoa, the former government official who led peace negotiations with the group, said “the worst-case scenario would be for the new government to close the ZUT, launch a military operation and try to capture or kill them. That would be a crime against humanity, because these people are unarmed.”

Between 2 and 4 August, days before De la Espriella’s inauguration, Novoa led journalists including the Guardian through the ZUT. The Office of the High Commissioner for Peace, where he worked, has since been absorbed into the newly created National Security Commission – a move expected to result in more than 200 job losses – and Novoa has resigned.
For now, at least, the ZUT remains in operation and has a small library run by Bríñez, who has a phoenix tattoo on her left shoulder as a symbol of her rebirth away from the armed conflict.

blocks.caption: No weapons are allowed inside the ZUT and soldiers guard it from a perimeter less than a mile away. Photograph: Daniela Díaz/The Guardian

blocks.text: “The hardest thing for me has been being away from my children,” said Bríñez, who has a seven-year-old daughter and a 10-year-old son and speaks to them on video calls, but will only be able to see them in person once her “transition” is complete, a process that includes vocational training and psychosocial support.
They were also supposed to receive financial support of about £425 a month, which had not yet been paid. In the meantime, some of them were planning to start a chicken-rearing business.

The 99 made up a small part of a group of about 1,000 combatants called Commandos of the Frontier – most of whom remain armed – and are part of the National Coordinator of the Bolivarian Army (CNEB), a former dissident faction of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc) with about 2,500 members which controls the border with Ecuador.

The Petro administration said negotiations were also under way with other members of the CNEB, who published an open letter addressed to De la Espriella saying they were willing to continue talks with him. It is not known whether the president responded.

blocks.caption: One of the works of graffiti in the ZUT painted by the former guerrillas. Photograph: Daniela Díaz/The Guardian

blocks.text: The CNEB’s chief “peace negotiator”, Geovany Andrés Rojas, known as “Araña” (Spider), had been in custody since February under a US extradition request for drug trafficking, which Petro had delayed. Last Wednesday, De la Espriella ordered extradition.

Although such groups emerged in the 1960s as leftwing rebels fighting government abuses and seeking revolution – followed soon afterwards by far-right paramilitary groups – ideology has long since been overtaken for most of them by economic interests, above all drug trafficking (Colombia is the world’s largest producer of cocaine) and illegal mining.

“Here in the ZUT, the vast majority were not in the group because of any ideological commitment, but for economic reasons,” said Novoa. “It even surprised us that most of them simply called the group ‘the company’.”

Petro repeatedly tried to negotiate peace agreements with larger groups. The armed factions took advantage of temporary ceasefires to continue expanding, a process that had already begun before he took office. They also clashed among themselves for control of territory and illicit economies, which many security experts say contributed to a rise in homicides, kidnappings and massacres.
“Total peace” was an attempt to address what the landmark 2016 peace deal between the government and the Farc failed to resolve, as other armed groups and Farc dissidents remained active.

Petro’s administration failed to reduce violence, which instead reached its worst levels in a decade, and to reach the disarmament stage with any of the gangs, apart from the 99 former combatants – who handed over their weapons only on the eve of an election that every poll indicated the government-backed candidate would lose.
“They [the government] told us: ‘If this works, you’re opening the door for other groups and will set an example,’” said Bríñez.
Some security experts saw the agreement as rushed.

blocks.caption: Former guerrillas in the ZUT have little to do and spend much of their time looking at their phones. Photograph: Daniela Díaz/The Guardian

blocks.text: “It was a somewhat irresponsible decision,” said Paula Tobo, a senior researcher at the thinktank Ideas for Peace Foundation, which published an extensive report on why Total Peace failed.

Tobo said the 99 were now in a “legal limbo” because their protection rested on decrees that could be revoked and there is no legal framework for their transition to civilian life. All of the Petro administration’s proposals to regulate surrenders failed in Congress and, under current law, anyone who has committed crimes such as kidnapping or drug trafficking is not eligible for amnesty.

“It’s positive that these people wanted to lay down their arms, but it really wasn’t the right time for the government to take that decision … The previous administration clearly put them at risk of this government suddenly deciding to abolish the ZUT and arrest them,” said Tobo.
The group wrote a letter to De la Espriella reaffirming its “irreversible decision to commit to peace” and inviting him to visit the ZUT. At the time of publication it had received no response.
The youngest member of the group, a 19-year-old who asked to be identified only as Adrián, said they wanted “to have a home, a family”.

However, he knows what he will do if things do not go according to plan. “Honestly, I’d take up arms again, because we’re keeping our side of the bargain and the government should do the same, shouldn’t it?” he said.
Daniela Díaz travelled to Valle del Guamuez at the invitation of the Colombian government’s former Office of the High Commissioner for Peace.

The Comelec en banc rejected the motion for reconsideration of the Moro Ako Party, affirming the earlier cancellation of its registration as a regional parliamentary political party for the September 14 regional elections.
In a resolution promulgated on Friday, August 28, the commission upheld its August 4 decision to grant a petition against the party over alleged misrepresentation.

How the BARMM vote works
How will those in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) vote?

Because this is a parliamentary election, they will vote for a regional political party and one district representative. Voters don’t get to choose the BARMM chief minister. Rather, the elected parliament will pick the chief minister.

The BARMM parliament will have 80 members. Forty seats will go to party representatives (from the regional political parties), 32 seats go to parliamentary district representatives, and eight seats are reserved for sectoral representatives.

blocks.text: Thirteen political parties faced off in Cotabato on Thursday, August 27, for the first BARMM Parliamentary Elections Debate organized by the Institute for Autonomy and Governance. Held at Notre Dame University, the historic face-off showcased competing platforms for the regional government ahead of the landmark polls.

The debates centered on socioeconomic reforms, service decentralization, and resolving clan feuds or rido. Candidates also clashed over Sulu’s exclusion, electoral integrity, and resisting national government interference.

The event ended with party-list groups signing posters to pledge their commitment to civil society advocacies. This included signing covenants of commitment with Duyog Bangsamoro and the Coalition for Social Accountability and Transparency. – Rappler.com

Delayed services an injustice to Bangsamoro — Loong

“Sang-ayon tayo sa decentralization kasi bakit natin i-centralize dito kung ang outcome ay kalahati ang nagagastos natin, kung ang outcome ay two years tayong delayed sa implementation. Because that is an injustice to the Bangsamoro people,” said engineer Don Mustapha Loong of the Progresibong Bangsamoro Party.
Loong defended decentralization as a way to make government services more efficient and responsive to communities.
He questioned the value of centralizing services when it results in lower spending outcomes and delays of up to two years in implementation.
Loong called the failure to deliver the gains of the Bangsamoro transition “the greatest injustice that could possibly happen.”
He said the “fruits of the revolution” may already be within reach, yet many Bangsamoro people remain unable to experience their benefits. – Angelle Matura

“We have to take care of taxpayers’ money. Every family, every working-class family, every month, nakikita nila sa payroll nila, tax withheld. Can you imagine that money could’ve gone to one more sack of rice, one week’s worth of grocery?” said Nur-Ainee Tan Lim Misuari of the Mahardika Party.

Lim called for greater accountability in the use of public funds, pointing to the underutilization of the block grant, limited absorptive capacity, and inefficiency in spending within the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.
She said the region needs leaders who can restrain themselves, put people first, and use public funds for the Bangsamoro.
“This is a government of failure,” Abdulhussein Kashim of Indigenous, Settles, Sama and Minorities Alliance Party described the situation bluntly.
He said the government has a strong legal foundation to deliver resources to the people but has failed to do so.
Despite the criticisms, Lim said there remains an opportunity for the Bangsamoro to “rise from the ashes,” particularly for undecided voters who are weighing their choices.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: PENSHOPPE Designer Lab announces first collaboration with Chicago-based Filipino streetwear brand ABAKADA
articles.summary: As PENSHOPPE celebrates its 40th anniversary, the brand marks the milestone by continuing to create opportunities for Filipino creativity to take center stage. This October, PENSHOPPE introduces…

blocks.text: Lifestyle | Fashion and Beauty
PENSHOPPE celebrates 40 years of fashion with a limited-edition collaboration that brings ABAKADA's Chicago-rooted Filipino streetwear to Manila this October 2026

As PENSHOPPE celebrates its 40th anniversary, the brand marks the milestone by continuing to create opportunities for Filipino creativity to take center stage. This October, PENSHOPPE introduces PENSHOPPE Designer Lab: ABAKADA, its first collaboration under the creative platform, bringing together PENSHOPPE and ABAKADA, the Chicago-based Filipino streetwear brand founded by Arvin Boyon and Calvin Calma in 2018.

PENSHOPPE Designer Lab is a creative platform created to bring PENSHOPPE together with distinct creative voices and develop limited-edition collections that explore new perspectives in fashion. For its first collaboration, the Designer Lab partners with ABAKADA, a brand that has built its identity around Filipino culture, contemporary streetwear, and the Filipino-American experience.

Founded in Chicago, ABAKADA has grown from its beginnings as a Filipino-American streetwear label into a brand making its mark in the US streetwear scene. Founders Arvin Boyon and Calvin Calma incorporate Filipino heritage, language, and cultural references into contemporary designs, creating a distinct streetwear identity rooted in where they come from.

For PENSHOPPE Designer Lab: ABAKADA, the two brands come together for a 23-piece limited-edition collection that blends ABAKADA’s Filipino-rooted streetwear identity with PENSHOPPE’s accessible approach to fashion. Featuring sporty and streetwear-inspired silhouettes, the collection brings together contemporary style and Filipino cultural influences.

The collaboration will be officially launched in October 2026 on the PENSHOPPE App and in select PENSHOPPE stores nationwide. An exclusive first look at select pieces will also be available for pre-order at the Purveyur Fair this September, ahead of the official launch.

As PENSHOPPE enters its 40th year, PENSHOPPE Designer Lab: ABAKADA reflects the brand's continued evolution while celebrating the Filipino creativity that connects communities across borders. From Chicago to Manila, the collaboration marks a new chapter in PENSHOPPE's 40-year story.
Follow PENSHOPPE on social media and download the PENSHOPPE App for more updates on PENSHOPPE Designer Lab: ABAKADA.

articles.title: Indonesian claims collegiate men’s singles crown
articles.summary: Gibran Berliangga of Indonesia made the most of his trip to the Philippines, capturing the collegiate men’s singles title of the PTTF Intercollegiate and Interscholastic Challenge on Friday evening…

blocks.text: Gibran Berliangga of Indonesia made the most of his trip to the Philippines, capturing the collegiate men’s singles title of the PTTF Intercollegiate and Interscholastic Challenge on Friday evening at the Home Court at Ayala Malls Manila Bay in Parañaque City.

The rising star from Jawa Barat defeated University of Makati’s EJ Yamson, 11-8, 11-9, 11-8, to claim the title in the tournament backed by the Huaching Foundation, Philippine Sports Commission, PLDT, Topcoms Marketing Inc., Mizuno Philippines, Cara Celine Dormtel, Gold Cross Security Agency, and Best Options Assistance Inc., along with Dino Jalandoni, Bombit Silva, and Eric Ongkauco.

Berliangga was among the more than 409 student-paddlers who took part in the biggest staging of the tournament to date, with participants coming from nearly all over the country, including the University of Mindanao.
Berliangga and Yamson earlier booked their spots in the semifinals with victories over University of Santo Tomas’ Jebb Datahan and De La Salle University’s Morrison Torres, respectively.
The Indonesian denied the Filipino upstart, Datahan, 11-4, 11-5, 11-9, while Yamson, a former DLSU Green Paddler, outlasted his former teammate Torres, 11-8, 11-13, 9-11, 13-11, 11-8.
The other completed events—the high school boys’ singles and boys’ doubles—went to the Philippines, with UST claiming the latter.

Top Filipino junior paddler Emmanuel Paculba Jr. stopped an Indonesian sweep of the men’s singles titles by taking the high school boys’ crown with a 6-11, 12-10, 11-8, 5-11, 11-7 victory over Muhammad Sayyid Sedi.

UST’s Ramon Canalin and Kieji Ridor completed their dream run with an 8-11, 11-6, 14-12, 7-11, 11-9 victory over Philippine Christian University’s top-seeded pair of NJ Marin and Kyle Ruedas in the doubles final.
Canalin and Ridor earned the right to represent the Junior Tiger Paddlers after sweeping Paul Agunod and Carl Sabandal, 11-9, 11-6, 11-9, in the semifinals.
Marin and Ruedas, meanwhile, defeated Indonesians Farel Deni Al Jabbar Nur and Muhammad Sayyid Sedi, 11-7, 11-7, 11-7, to arrange their finals showdown with the eventual champions.
Action in the team events and the playoffs for the collegiate women’s singles, men’s and women’s doubles, and high school girls’ singles and doubles was ongoing as of this writing.
Selected matches will be streamed live on the new and improved CPlay app and the One Sports YouTube channel.

articles.title: CJ Perez on Gilas takeover: ‘I just did my thing’
articles.summary: CJ Perez said there was no conscious effort on his part to take over for Gilas Pilipinas in its 82-81 win over Jordan, noting that he simply played his game, and the breakout performance followed.…

blocks.text: At A Glance

items: CJ Perez said that there wasn't any conscious effort on his part to take over for Gilas Pilipinas in its 82-81 win over Jordan, noting that he only played his game and the breakout performance simply followed.

blocks.text: CJ Perez emerges as Gilas Pilipinas' sparkplug in its narrow win over Jordan. (FIBA)
CJ Perez said there was no conscious effort on his part to take over for Gilas Pilipinas in its 82-81 win over Jordan, noting that he simply played his game, and the breakout performance followed.
The San Miguel Beer star came alive when it mattered most, scoring all but two of his 16 points in the fourth quarter and overtime to emerge as a key spark in the Nationals' hard-fought victory.
“I just did my thing. No one told me to take over but I took it. I took the risk,” said Perez after the game.
“Pag mga ganung sitwasyon di ko na masyado naiisip (to take over) pero syempre sa kumpyansa ng mga teammates ko kasi nakakashoot na nga ako so binigay nila,” he added in a separate interview.

More than the scoring outburst, Perez made his biggest play down the stretch the stretch when Jordan’s defense finally collapsed on him, allowing him to find a wide-open Kevin Quiambao for the go-ahead triple with 11.7 seconds left.
“Ang mga coaches talaga nag trust lang talaga sila. They are telling me to just attack the basket. Pag nagtitouch ako ng paint naoopen yung iba and then nakakatira ako,” recalled Perez.
“Nasu-shoot ko kasi yung layup so nag collapse sila so luckily, nandun si KQ nakita ko siya and he made the shot. Sobrang kumpyansa ni KQ. I'm proud of him,” he added.

articles.title: Partial collapse of Aquino Bridge feared as rains persist in Tarlac City
articles.summary: TARLAC CITY — Authorities are closely monitoring bridges, roads, and other critical infrastructure in Tarlac City amid fears of further damage as continuous rains persist in the area following the…

blocks.text: TARLAC CITY — Authorities are closely monitoring bridges, roads, and other critical infrastructure in Tarlac City amid fears of further damage as continuous rains persist in the area following the partial collapse of Aquino Bridge.
Among these infrastructure is the Aquino Bridge, which was closed to all motorists after a portion of the structure collapsed at around 11:56 p.m. on August 28.

blocks.caption:
INFRASTRUCTURE AT RISK: Authorities continue to monitor bridges and other critical infrastructure in Tarlac City as heavy rains persist, following the partial collapse of Aquino Bridge and the threat of further flooding and damage.
(Photo courtesy of Tarlac City Government via Liezle Inigo)

blocks.text: INFRASTRUCTURE AT RISK: Authorities continue to monitor bridges and other critical infrastructure in Tarlac City as heavy rains persist, following the partial collapse of Aquino Bridge and the threat of further flooding and damage. (Photo courtesy of Tarlac City Government via Liezle Inigo)
The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) is conducting a technical assessment to determine the extent of the damage and the appropriate intervention needed to restore the bridge.
The city government is also closely monitoring Agana Bridge, which could face increased traffic pressure as motorists are being diverted there following the closure of Aquino Bridge.
Traffic management measures and alternative routes are being coordinated with the police, provincial government, and neighboring municipalities, particularly for trucks, buses, and heavy equipment.

blocks.caption:
INFRASTRUCTURE AT RISK: Authorities continue to monitor bridges and other critical infrastructure in Tarlac City as heavy rains persist, following the partial collapse of Aquino Bridge and the threat of further flooding and damage.
(Photo courtesy of Tarlac City Government via Liezle Inigo)

blocks.text: Flood-prone communities are likewise being monitored as the rains continue. The city government has conducted preemptive evacuation of families in Zone 3, San Isidro Tibag, Burot, and San Luis, while pumping stations, sandbagging operations, and other flood-control measures remain in operation.

The disruption caused by the bridge damage has also affected water service in several barangays, with San Isidro, Tibag, Baras-Baras, Dolores, Care, and Sapang Maragul experiencing low water pressure to no water due to damage to the water line crossing the bridge.
The city government has prepared a water truck as an augmentation measure.
Meanwhile, authorities appealed to residents to avoid unnecessary travel, keep children indoors, and rely only on official advisories.
City emergency responders and health centers remain on standby as the local government continues monitoring conditions and providing assistance to affected families.
